06 Externalized Configuration · 08 REST APIs with Spring MVC

docs.title: 08 · Building REST APIs with Spring MVC
1. Introduction & Why It Matters
docs.text:
Almost every grocery service exposes HTTP: the Angular web app and Flutter mobile app call the gateway, sellers upload catalogs, delivery partners update statuses, Razorpay calls our webhooks. Spring MVC is the servlet-based web framework that turns those HTTP requests into method calls — and it's still the default choice for Boot services, especially now that virtual threads remove most of the scalability argument for reactive stacks.

Getting REST APIs right matters beyond "it returns JSON":

  • Correct semantics (status codes, methods, headers) let clients, proxies and caches behave correctly — e.g. a POST that returns 201 Created with a Location, or 409 Conflict when a cart was modified on another device.
  • Stable contracts — DTOs separate from entities, so a JPA refactor doesn't break the mobile app still installed on 2 million phones.
  • Performance and safety — pagination limits, upload size limits, streaming for large files.
  • Clean layering — controllers do HTTP only; the four-layer pattern keeps business logic testable.

This chapter builds the cart-service API end to end: product listing with pagination and filters, cart operations with optimistic concurrency via ETags, a custom argument resolver for the current customer, a pincode serviceability interceptor, CORS for the web app, seller CSV upload and invoice download streaming. Validation (Chapter 09), error handling (Chapter 10), JSON (Chapter 11) and API versioning/design (Chapter 20) build on it.

docs.title: Who should read which section
docs.text: Band Focus B1 · 0–2 yrs Parts 1, 2, 4 — controllers, mappings, parameters, status codes B2 · 2–5 yrs Parts 2, 5 — ResponseEntity, pagination, upload/download, CORS, interceptors vs filters B3 · 5–8 yrs Parts 3, 5, 6 — DispatcherServlet internals, argument resolvers, message converters, streaming B4 · 8–12 yrs Parts 6, 7, 8 — API standards, concurrency control, performance, Boot 4 changes B5 · 12–15+ yrs Parts 8, 9 — API governance and platform conventions

docs.title: 2.1 REST in one table
docs.text:
Method Semantics Safe Idempotent Typical success status GET Read ✅ ✅ 200 HEAD Read headers only ✅ ✅ 200 POST Create / non-idempotent action ❌ ❌ 201 (+ Location), 202, 200 PUT Replace full resource ❌ ✅ 200 or 204 PATCH Partial update ❌ Not necessarily 200 or 204 DELETE Remove ❌ ✅ 204 OPTIONS Capabilities (CORS preflight) ✅ ✅ 200/204

Common error statuses: 400 (malformed/invalid), 401 (not authenticated), 403 (not allowed), 404 (not found), 405 (method not allowed), 406 (can't produce requested type), 409 (state conflict), 412 (precondition failed — ETag mismatch), 413 (payload too large), 415 (unsupported media type), 422 (semantically invalid), 428 (precondition required), 429 (rate limited), 500, 502/503/504.

docs.title: 2.2 Controllers
docs.text:
• @RestController = @Controller + @ResponseBody on every method: return values are written to the response body via message converters.
  • @Controller without @ResponseBody returns view names (server-side rendering — rare in API services).

docs.title: 2.3 Request mapping
docs.text:
Annotation Example @RequestMapping (class level) @RequestMapping("/api/carts") @GetMapping, @PostMapping, @PutMapping, @PatchMapping, @DeleteMapping @GetMapping("/{cartId}") Narrowing attributes consumes, produces, params, headers

Path patterns (Spring's PathPatternParser, the default since Boot 2.6):

Pattern Matches /products/{sku} One segment captured as sku /products/{sku:[A-Z0-9-]+} With regex /files/{*path} Captures the rest of the path /static/** Any sub-path (only at the end)

Trailing slashes

Since Spring Framework 6, /api/carts/ does not match /api/carts by default. Clients must be exact, or you handle it at the gateway/with a filter.

docs.title: 2.4 Reading request data
docs.text:
Annotation Source Example @PathVariable URI template @PathVariable String cartId @RequestParam Query string / form @RequestParam(defaultValue = "20") int size @RequestHeader Header @RequestHeader("X-Pincode") String pincode @CookieValue Cookie @CookieValue("session") String s @RequestBody Body via message converter @RequestBody AddItemRequest req @ModelAttribute (implicit for non-simple types) Query/form params bound to an object ProductFilter filter @RequestPart Multipart part @RequestPart MultipartFile file @MatrixVariable ;key=value in path rare Special types HttpServletRequest, Principal, Locale, UriComponentsBuilder, Pageable —

Records as query objects: ProductFilter(String category, BigDecimal maxPrice) binds ?category=dairy&maxPrice=100 through its constructor.

docs.title: 2.5 Responses
docs.text: Return type Behaviour Any object/record Serialized with status 200 (or @ResponseStatus) ResponseEntity<T> Full control: status, headers, body void + @ResponseStatus(NO_CONTENT) Empty body ProblemDetail / ErrorResponse RFC 9457 error body (Chapter 10) StreamingResponseBody Write directly to the output stream asynchronously ResponseEntity<Resource> File download SseEmitter, ResponseBodyEmitter Server-sent events / streaming (Chapter 32) Callable, DeferredResult, CompletableFuture Async processing (less needed with virtual threads)

docs.title: 2.6 Content negotiation and message converters
docs.text:
HttpMessageConverters turn bodies into objects and back: Jackson for JSON, String, byte arrays, resources, form data, XML (if Jackson XML present). The chosen converter depends on:

  • Request: Content-Type header → which converter can read → 415 if none.
  • Response: Accept header ∩ produces ∩ converters that can write the return type → 406 if none.

docs.title: 2.7 Pagination, sorting, filtering
docs.text:
• Spring Data's Pageable resolves ?page=0&size=20&sort=price,asc automatically.
  • Don't serialize Page/PageImpl directly — its JSON structure isn't a stable contract (Spring Data warns about it). Return your own PageResponse<T> record, or enable Spring Data's DTO-based serialization (@EnableSpringDataWebSupport(pageSerializationMode = VIA_DTO)).
  • Always cap page size (spring.data.web.pageable.max-page-size).
  • For deep/infinite scrolling, prefer keyset (cursor) pagination (Chapter 13) over large offsets.

docs.title: 2.8 Filters vs interceptors vs argument resolvers vs advice
docs.text: Mechanism Level Sees Use for Servlet Filter Servlet container, before Spring MVC Raw request/response Security, correlation IDs, compression, request logging HandlerInterceptor Spring MVC, around handler Request + chosen handler method Per-endpoint cross-cutting checks (pincode serviceability, MDC) HandlerMethodArgumentResolver Spring MVC, per parameter Request + parameter metadata Custom parameter types (@CurrentCustomer) @ControllerAdvice / ResponseBodyAdvice Spring MVC Exceptions / response bodies Error mapping, response wrapping AOP (Chapter 04) Any bean Method invocation Business-level concerns (idempotency, audit)

docs.title: 2.9 CORS
docs.text: Browsers block cross-origin calls (Angular on https://www.grocery.in → API on https://api.grocery.in) unless the server returns CORS headers. Configure globally via WebMvcConfigurer.addCorsMappings (or with Spring Security's CorsConfigurationSource when Security is present — Chapter 17), or per controller with @CrossOrigin. Mobile apps aren't subject to CORS.

docs.title: 2.10 The four-layer pattern in web code
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    C["Controller<br/>HTTP: mapping, params, status,<br/>headers, request/response DTOs"] --> D["Delegate<br/>orchestration: map DTO↔domain,<br/>call services, assemble views,<br/>idempotency boundary"]
    D --> S["Service<br/>business rules, transactions,<br/>domain events"]
    S --> R["Repository<br/>persistence"]

Rules: controllers never touch repositories or entities; services never see HTTP types; delegates never contain business rules.

docs.title: 3.1 DispatcherServlet request flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client
    participant F as Filter chain (Security, correlation...)
    participant DS as DispatcherServlet
    participant HM as HandlerMapping<br/>(RequestMappingHandlerMapping)
    participant I as HandlerInterceptors
    participant HA as HandlerAdapter<br/>(RequestMappingHandlerAdapter)
    participant AR as ArgumentResolvers
    participant C as Controller method
    participant RV as ReturnValueHandlers
    participant MC as HttpMessageConverters
    participant ER as HandlerExceptionResolvers

    Client->>F: HTTP request
    F->>DS: doDispatch
    DS->>HM: getHandler(request)
    HM-->>DS: HandlerExecutionChain (method + interceptors)
    DS->>I: preHandle
    DS->>HA: handle
    HA->>AR: resolve each parameter<br/>(@PathVariable, @RequestBody → MC read, validation)
    HA->>C: invoke
    C-->>HA: return value
    HA->>RV: handleReturnValue<br/>(@ResponseBody → MC write, content negotiation)
    DS->>I: postHandle
    alt exception anywhere
        DS->>ER: resolveException<br/>(@ExceptionHandler, ResponseStatus, defaults)
    end
    DS->>I: afterCompletion
    DS-->>Client: response

Key classes:

  • DispatcherServlet — front controller registered by Boot at /.
  • RequestMappingHandlerMapping — at startup scans @RequestMapping methods into RequestMappingInfos; at runtime matches path, method, params, headers, consumes, produces, and picks the most specific.
  • RequestMappingHandlerAdapter — invokes the method via ServletInvocableHandlerMethod, using argument resolvers and return value handlers.
  • RequestResponseBodyMethodProcessor — handles @RequestBody/@ResponseBody with message converters and RequestBodyAdvice/ResponseBodyAdvice.
  • HandlerExceptionResolverComposite — ExceptionHandlerExceptionResolver (@ExceptionHandler), ResponseStatusExceptionResolver, DefaultHandlerExceptionResolver.

docs.title: 3.2 Choosing the handler method
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[GET /api/products/ATTA-5KG<br/>Accept: application/json] --> B[PathPattern matching<br/>all RequestMappingInfos]
    B --> C{method matches?}
    C -- none --> X405[405 Method Not Allowed]
    C --> D{consumes matches Content-Type?}
    D -- none --> X415[415 Unsupported Media Type]
    D --> E{produces matches Accept?}
    E -- none --> X406[406 Not Acceptable]
    E --> F[sort candidates by specificity<br/>fewer wildcards, more conditions]
    F --> G{tie between top two?}
    G -- yes --> XA[IllegalStateException:<br/>Ambiguous handler methods]
    G -- no --> H[handler found]

docs.title: 3.3 Where virtual threads fit
docs.text: With spring.threads.virtual.enabled=true, Tomcat dispatches each request on a new virtual thread. Blocking calls (JDBC, RestClient) unmount the virtual thread instead of blocking a platform thread. The MVC programming model is unchanged — that's the point. Watch for pinning (long synchronized blocks around I/O in older libraries) and bound concurrency at downstream pools (Chapter 25).

docs.title: 4.1 A product catalog controller
4.2 Testing the controller
5. Hands-On Code — Level 2 (Intermediate) & Level 3 (Advanced)
docs.text: From here on the cart-service uses the four layers. Packages: web, delegate, service, repository.

docs.title: 5.1 Level 2 — DTOs and the four layers
5.2 Level 2 — Pagination, sorting and filtering
5.3 Level 2 — File upload and download
5.4 Level 3 — Custom argument resolver: @CurrentCustomer
docs.text:
Until Chapter 17 introduces JWTs, customer identity arrives in a gateway-set header. Controllers shouldn't parse headers repeatedly.

in/grocery/platform/web/CurrentCustomer.java
package in.grocery.platform.web;

import java.lang.annotation.ElementType;
import java.lang.annotation.Retention;
import java.lang.annotation.RetentionPolicy;
import java.lang.annotation.Target;

@Target(ElementType.PARAMETER)
@Retention(RetentionPolicy.RUNTIME)
public @interface CurrentCustomer {}
in/grocery/platform/web/CustomerContext.java
package in.grocery.platform.web;

public record CustomerContext(String customerId, String pincode, String channel) {}
in/grocery/platform/web/CurrentCustomerArgumentResolver.java
package in.grocery.platform.web;

import java.util.regex.Pattern;
import org.springframework.core.MethodParameter;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.web.bind.support.WebDataBinderFactory;
import org.springframework.web.context.request.NativeWebRequest;
import org.springframework.web.method.support.HandlerMethodArgumentResolver;
import org.springframework.web.method.support.ModelAndViewContainer;
import org.springframework.web.server.ResponseStatusException;

public class CurrentCustomerArgumentResolver implements HandlerMethodArgumentResolver {

    private static final Pattern CUSTOMER = Pattern.compile("C-[0-9]{1,12}");
    private static final Pattern PINCODE = Pattern.compile("[1-9][0-9]{5}");

    @Override
    public boolean supportsParameter(MethodParameter parameter) {                           // (1)!
        return parameter.hasParameterAnnotation(CurrentCustomer.class)
                && parameter.getParameterType().equals(CustomerContext.class);
    }

    @Override
    public Object resolveArgument(MethodParameter parameter, ModelAndViewContainer mav,
                                  NativeWebRequest request, WebDataBinderFactory binderFactory) {
        String id = request.getHeader("X-Customer-Id");
        if (id == null || !CUSTOMER.matcher(id).matches()) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.UNAUTHORIZED, "Missing or invalid customer identity");
        }
        String pincode = request.getHeader("X-Pincode");
        if (pincode != null && !PINCODE.matcher(pincode).matches()) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "Invalid X-Pincode");
        }
        String channel = request.getHeader("X-Channel");
        return new CustomerContext(id, pincode, channel == null ? "web" : channel);
    }
}
  1. Result of supportsParameter is cached per parameter — keep it cheap and deterministic.
in/grocery/platform/web/GroceryWebMvcConfig.java
package in.grocery.platform.web;

import java.util.List;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Configuration;
import org.springframework.web.method.support.HandlerMethodArgumentResolver;
import org.springframework.web.servlet.config.annotation.WebMvcConfigurer;

@Configuration(proxyBeanMethods = false)
public class GroceryWebMvcConfig implements WebMvcConfigurer {                               // (1)!

    @Override
    public void addArgumentResolvers(List<HandlerMethodArgumentResolver> resolvers) {
        resolvers.add(new CurrentCustomerArgumentResolver());

}

docs.title: 5.5 Level 3 — Interceptor: pincode serviceability
docs.text:
Only some endpoints need a serviceable pincode (add-to-cart, checkout). An interceptor can inspect the handler method's annotations, which a filter can't.

in/grocery/platform/web/RequiresServiceablePincode.java
package in.grocery.platform.web;

import java.lang.annotation.ElementType;
import java.lang.annotation.Retention;
import java.lang.annotation.RetentionPolicy;
import java.lang.annotation.Target;

@Target({ElementType.METHOD, ElementType.TYPE})
@Retention(RetentionPolicy.RUNTIME)
public @interface RequiresServiceablePincode {}
in/grocery/platform/web/ServiceabilityInterceptor.java
package in.grocery.platform.web;

import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest;
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletResponse;
import org.springframework.core.annotation.AnnotatedElementUtils;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.web.method.HandlerMethod;
import org.springframework.web.server.ResponseStatusException;
import org.springframework.web.servlet.HandlerInterceptor;

public class ServiceabilityInterceptor implements HandlerInterceptor {

    public interface ServiceabilityChecker { boolean isServiceable(String pincode); }  // cached lookup, Chapter 21

    private final ServiceabilityChecker checker;

    public ServiceabilityInterceptor(ServiceabilityChecker checker) {
        this.checker = checker;
    }

    @Override
    public boolean preHandle(HttpServletRequest req, HttpServletResponse res, Object handler) {
        if (!(handler instanceof HandlerMethod hm)) return true;                               // (1)!
        boolean required = hm.hasMethodAnnotation(RequiresServiceablePincode.class)
                || AnnotatedElementUtils.hasAnnotation(hm.getBeanType(), RequiresServiceablePincode.class);
        if (!required) return true;

        String pincode = req.getHeader("X-Pincode");
        if (pincode == null) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.PRECONDITION_REQUIRED, "X-Pincode header is required");
        }
        if (!checker.isServiceable(pincode)) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY,
                    "We don't deliver to " + pincode + " yet");
        }
        return true;
    }
}
  1. Static resources and other handler types pass through.
GroceryWebMvcConfig.java (continued)
@Override
public void addInterceptors(InterceptorRegistry registry) {
    registry.addInterceptor(new ServiceabilityInterceptor(checker))
            .addPathPatterns("/api/**")
            .excludePathPatterns("/api/public/**");
}
Interceptor: pincode serviceability (snippet)

@Override
public void addCorsMappings(CorsRegistry registry) {
    registry.addMapping("/api/**")
            .allowedOrigins(corsProps.allowedOrigins().toArray(String[]::new))    // (1)!
            .allowedMethods("GET", "POST", "PUT", "PATCH", "DELETE")
            .allowedHeaders("Content-Type", "Authorization", "X-Pincode", "Idempotency-Key", "If-Match")
            .exposedHeaders("ETag", "Location", "X-Request-Id")                   // (2)!
            .allowCredentials(true)
            .maxAge(3600);
}
  1. Explicit origins. Never * together with credentials (browsers reject it) — and never reflect arbitrary Origin values.
  2. Without exposedHeaders, Angular can't read ETag from the response — a common cause of "concurrency doesn't work in the browser".

With Spring Security

Once Spring Security is added (Chapter 17), configure CORS through http.cors(...) and a CorsConfigurationSource bean so preflight requests are handled before authentication.

docs.title: 5.7 Level 3 — Filters for raw HTTP concerns
Optimistic concurrency with ETag / If-Match
docs.text:
A customer edits their cart on the phone and the laptop simultaneously. Without protection, the last write silently wins and items disappear. HTTP has a standard answer: conditional requests.

sequenceDiagram
    participant Phone
    participant Laptop
    participant API as cart-service

    Phone->>API: GET /api/carts/c1
    API-->>Phone: 200 ETag: "7"
    Laptop->>API: GET /api/carts/c1
    API-->>Laptop: 200 ETag: "7"
    Phone->>API: PATCH /items/MILK-1L  If-Match: "7"
    API-->>Phone: 200 ETag: "8"
    Laptop->>API: PATCH /items/ATTA-5KG  If-Match: "7"
    API-->>Laptop: 412 Precondition Failed (current version 8)
    Laptop->>API: GET /api/carts/c1
    API-->>Laptop: 200 ETag: "8"  — UI refreshes, user retries
in/grocery/cart/web/CartCommandController.java
package in.grocery.cart.web;

import in.grocery.cart.delegate.CartDelegate;
import in.grocery.cart.web.dto.CartDtos.CartView;
import in.grocery.cart.web.dto.CartDtos.UpdateQuantityRequest;
import in.grocery.platform.web.CurrentCustomer;
import in.grocery.platform.web.CustomerContext;
import in.grocery.platform.web.RequiresServiceablePincode;
import java.util.regex.Matcher;
import java.util.regex.Pattern;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PatchMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PathVariable;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestBody;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestHeader;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;
import org.springframework.web.server.ResponseStatusException;

@RestController
@RequestMapping("/api/v1/carts")
class CartCommandController {

    private static final Pattern STRONG_ETAG = Pattern.compile("^\"(\\d{1,18})\"$");

    private final CartDelegate delegate;

    CartCommandController(CartDelegate delegate) {
        this.delegate = delegate;
    }

    @GetMapping("/{cartId}")
    ResponseEntity<CartView> get(@PathVariable String cartId, @CurrentCustomer CustomerContext customer) {
        CartView cart = delegate.getCartFor(customer.customerId(), cartId);                    // (1)!
        return ResponseEntity.ok().eTag(etag(cart.version())).body(cart);                      // (2)!
    }

    @PatchMapping("/{cartId}/items/{sku}")
    @RequiresServiceablePincode
    ResponseEntity<CartView> updateQuantity(@PathVariable String cartId,
                                            @PathVariable String sku,
                                            @RequestHeader(value = "If-Match", required = false) String ifMatch,
                                            @RequestBody UpdateQuantityRequest body,
                                            @CurrentCustomer CustomerContext customer) {
        long expectedVersion = parseIfMatch(ifMatch);                                          // (3)!
        CartView cart = delegate.updateQuantityFor(customer.customerId(), cartId, sku, body.quantity(), expectedVersion);
        return ResponseEntity.ok().eTag(etag(cart.version())).body(cart);
    }

    static long parseIfMatch(String ifMatch) {
        if (ifMatch == null) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.PRECONDITION_REQUIRED, "If-Match header is required"); // 428
        }
        Matcher m = STRONG_ETAG.matcher(ifMatch.strip());
        if (!m.matches()) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "If-Match must be a strong ETag like \"7\"");
        }
        return Long.parseLong(m.group(1));
    }

    private static String etag(long version) {
        return "\"" + version + "\"";
    }
}
  1. Delegate checks the cart belongs to the customer — return 404, not 403, for other customers' carts to avoid confirming existence.
  2. For GET requests returning a ResponseEntity with an ETag, Spring's HttpEntityMethodProcessor compares it with If-None-Match and sends 304 Not Modified without a body automatically — saves mobile data on polling. (For other return types, use WebRequest.checkNotModified(etag).)
  3. Requiring If-Match (428) on mutations forces clients to participate in concurrency control. Weak ETags (W/"7") are rejected.
in/grocery/cart/delegate/CartDelegate.java (additions)
public CartView getCartFor(String customerId, String cartId) {
    Cart cart = carts.get(cartId);
    if (!cart.customerId().equals(customerId)) throw new CartNotFoundException(cartId);
    return toView(carts.price(cart));
}

public CartView updateQuantityFor(String customerId, String cartId, String sku, int qty, long expectedVersion) {
    Cart cart = carts.get(cartId);
    if (!cart.customerId().equals(customerId)) throw new CartNotFoundException(cartId);
    if (cart.version() != expectedVersion) throw new CartVersionConflict(cartId, expectedVersion); // → 412
    return toView(carts.price(carts.updateQuantity(cartId, sku, qty)));                           // repo CAS covers races
}

docs.title: 7. Spring Boot 3 vs 4 & Migration
Migration checklist
docs.text:
• Switch starter names; fix @WebMvcTest/MockMvc imports.
  • Replace @MockBean with @MockitoBean (do it on 3.5 first).
  • Remove any @EnableWebMvc that crept in (it disables Boot's MVC setup in both versions).
  • Test all endpoints' JSON with Jackson 3 (date formats, nulls, enums) — contract tests (Chapter 28).
  • Decide whether to adopt built-in API versioning or keep path-based /v1/.
  • Check Servlet 6.1 behaviour changes for filters dealing with request/response wrappers.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
1. Controllers do HTTP only; four-layer pattern everywhere.
  2. Request/response DTOs as records, never entities.
  3. Correct status codes and headers: 201 + Location, 204, 409/412/428, ETag.
  4. Bound everything: page size, upload size, request header size, request timeouts.
  5. Stream large payloads (StreamingResponseBody, InputStream), never buffer.
  6. WebMvcConfigurer, not @EnableWebMvc.
  7. Interceptors for handler-aware checks; filters for raw HTTP concerns; argument resolvers for context objects.
  8. Stable page contract (PageResponse) and whitelisted sort fields.
  9. Explicit CORS origins and exposed headers.
  10. Return 404 for resources the caller isn't allowed to see where existence itself is sensitive.

docs.title: Anti-patterns
docs.text:
❌ Returning JPA entities

Anti-patterns (snippet)
@GetMapping("/{id}") Order get(@PathVariable Long id) { return orderRepository.findById(id).orElseThrow(); }
// lazy-loading exceptions, infinite recursion, leaks internal fields, couples API to schema

✅ Delegate maps to an OrderView record.

❌ Business logic in controllers (if (total > 499) fee = 0) — untestable without HTTP, duplicated across endpoints.

❌ 200 OK with {"success": false} — breaks every HTTP-aware tool.

❌ @RequestParam Map<String,String> for everything — no contract, no validation.

❌ @EnableWebMvc on a config class to "customize MVC" — loses Boot's defaults.

❌ Unbounded ?size= or offset pagination for infinite scroll on huge tables.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix 404 for an endpoint that exists Controller outside scanned package; trailing slash; context path Check package, exact path, server.servlet.context-path 405 Wrong HTTP method or mapping collision Check mappings (/actuator/mappings) 415 Missing/wrong Content-Type Send application/json; check consumes 406 Accept not producible (e.g. XML requested) Fix client Accept or add converter HttpMessageNotReadableException Malformed JSON / type mismatch Map to 400 with details (Chapter 10) Ambiguous handler methods Two mappings equally specific Narrow with params/headers/produces or restructure Location shows http:// or internal host Proxy headers ignored server.forward-headers-strategy + trusted proxies Angular can't read ETag CORS exposedHeaders missing Expose headers MaxUploadSizeExceededException Multipart limits Tune limits; map to 413 Streaming download times out Async request timeout spring.mvc.async.request-timeout Argument resolver never called Registered after a built-in resolver that claims the type Use a dedicated type/annotation; check order

docs.title: Production checklist
docs.text:
• All endpoints use DTO records; no entities in responses
  • Status codes and headers reviewed (create, delete, conflict, precondition)
  • Pagination capped; sort fields whitelisted
  • Upload/header/body limits set; large responses streamed
  • CORS explicit; exposed headers set
  • Forward headers configured behind ingress
  • /actuator/mappings reviewed for unintended endpoints
  • Web slice tests for each controller (happy path + error statuses)

docs.title: B1 · 0–2 years
docs.text:
B1 · @Controller vs @RestController?

Short answer: @RestController = @Controller + @ResponseBody; return values are serialized to the body. @Controller returns view names unless methods use @ResponseBody.

B1 · @PathVariable vs @RequestParam?

Short answer: Path variables come from the URI path (/products/{sku}); request params from the query string or form (?category=dairy).

B1 · What status code should a successful POST that creates a resource return?

Short answer: 201 Created with a Location header pointing to the new resource.

B1 · What is ResponseEntity?

Short answer: A return type giving full control over status, headers and body.

B1 · PUT vs PATCH?

Short answer: PUT replaces the whole resource and is idempotent; PATCH applies a partial update.

B1 · Why not return JPA entities from controllers?

Short answer: Couples API to schema, risks lazy-loading exceptions and recursion, exposes internal fields. Use DTOs.

docs.title: B2 · 2–5 years
docs.text:
B2 · Filter vs interceptor — when to use which?

Short answer: Filters run in the servlet container before MVC, for raw HTTP concerns (security, correlation, headers). Interceptors run inside MVC and know the handler method — use them for handler-aware checks.

B2 · How does content negotiation work?

Short answer: Spring matches the Accept header and produces against converters that can write the return type; the request Content-Type selects the reader. Failures yield 406/415.

B2 · How do you implement pagination in Spring MVC?

Short answer: Accept Pageable (Spring Data) with defaults and a max page size, return a stable page DTO, whitelist sort fields, and use keyset pagination for deep scrolling.

B2 · How do you handle large file uploads and downloads?

Short answer: Multipart limits, stream MultipartFile.getInputStream(), validate content, process asynchronously if heavy (202). For downloads use StreamingResponseBody or Resource with proper Content-Disposition.

B2 · How do you configure CORS for an Angular app?

Short answer: WebMvcConfigurer.addCorsMappings with explicit origins, methods, allowed/exposed headers, credentials, max age — or via Spring Security's CORS config when Security is present.

B2 · Why is @EnableWebMvc usually a mistake in Boot?

Short answer: It imports DelegatingWebMvcConfiguration, which makes Boot's WebMvcAutoConfiguration back off — you lose Boot's converters, formatting, static resource handling and properties.

docs.title: B3 · 5–8 years
docs.text:
B3 · Walk through the DispatcherServlet request lifecycle.

Short answer: Filters → DispatcherServlet.doDispatch → HandlerMapping finds handler + interceptors → preHandle → HandlerAdapter resolves arguments (message converters, validation), invokes method, handles return value (converters, content negotiation) → postHandle → exception resolvers if needed → afterCompletion.

B3 · How does RequestMappingHandlerMapping pick among multiple matching methods?

Short answer: Builds RequestMappingInfos at startup; at request time filters by pattern, method, params, headers, consumes, produces; sorts by specificity; throws if the top two are equally specific.

B3 · How would you add a custom controller parameter type?

Short answer: Implement HandlerMethodArgumentResolver, register via WebMvcConfigurer.addArgumentResolvers. Keep supportsParameter cheap; custom resolvers run after built-ins for most types, so use a dedicated type or annotation.

B3 · How do ETags and conditional requests work in Spring MVC?

Short answer: Set ETag on responses; WebRequest.checkNotModified(etag) handles If-None-Match → 304. For updates, compare If-Match with the current version → 412 on mismatch, 428 if required and missing. ShallowEtagHeaderFilter computes ETags from body hashes but saves only bandwidth, not server work.

B3 · What changes for Spring MVC with virtual threads?

Short answer: Each request runs on a virtual thread; blocking I/O is cheap; thread pool size stops being the bottleneck — downstream pools become it. Watch pinning, ThreadLocal-heavy libraries, and unbounded concurrency hitting databases.

docs.title: B4 · 8–12 years
docs.text:
B4 · How do you prevent lost updates in a REST API?

Short answer: Versioned resources with optimistic locking, exposed as strong ETags; require If-Match on mutations (428 if missing, 412 on mismatch); repository does compare-and-set; clients refetch and retry. For money-moving operations, add idempotency keys (Chapter 04).

B4 · What web standards would you enforce across 26 services?

Short answer: Resource naming, versioning, error format (RFC 9457), pagination contract, idempotency keys for creates, ETags for mutable resources, header conventions, limits, CORS policy, OpenAPI specs with linting, contract tests, and a platform web library with resolvers/interceptors.

B4 · Spring MVC or WebFlux for a new grocery service in 2026?

Short answer: MVC with virtual threads by default — simpler code, debugging, and ecosystem (JPA, JDBC). WebFlux where streaming/backpressure is intrinsic (live tracking feeds, very high fan-out gateways) or with a reactive data stack end-to-end. (Chapter 31.)

docs.title: B5 · 12–15+ years
docs.text:
B5 · How do you evolve APIs used by mobile apps you can't force-upgrade?

Short answer: Additive changes by default, tolerant readers, explicit versioning for breaking changes, sunset headers and telemetry on version usage, BFF/gateway adaptation, minimum supported app version enforced gracefully, and contract tests against recorded client expectations.

B5 · Where should cross-cutting HTTP concerns live: gateway, platform library, or each service?

Short answer: Edge concerns (TLS, rate limiting, WAF, coarse auth, routing) at the gateway; request-context, error format, correlation, fine-grained authorization in a platform library; business rules in services. Avoid duplicating the same check in all three.

docs.title: Scenario questions
docs.text:
Scenario · Customers report items vanishing from carts

Logs show concurrent PUT /carts/{id} from app and web, each sending the full cart. Last write wins. Fix: move to item-level PATCH endpoints, version the cart, require If-Match, return 412 with the current cart, update clients to refetch-and-merge, and add a metric for 412 rate.

Scenario · Location headers point to http://cart-service:8080/... in production

The service is behind an ingress terminating TLS. Without server.forward-headers-strategy, UriComponentsBuilder uses the internal host/scheme. Configure framework (or native) and trust the ingress's forwarded headers only.

docs.title: Coding exercise
docs.text:
Exercise · Delivery slot API

Implement GET /api/delivery/slots?pincode=560034&date=2026-10-20 returning available slots, and POST /api/delivery/slots/{slotId}/holds that holds a slot for a cart, returning 201 with Location, 409 if full. Use a record for query params, the four layers (in-memory service is fine), and write @WebMvcTest tests for 200, 201, 409 and 400 (invalid date).

Solution DeliverySlotController.java
package in.grocery.delivery.web;

import in.grocery.delivery.delegate.SlotDelegate;
import in.grocery.delivery.delegate.SlotView;
import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.util.List;
import org.springframework.format.annotation.DateTimeFormat;
import org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PathVariable;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PostMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestBody;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;
import org.springframework.web.util.UriComponentsBuilder;

@RestController
@RequestMapping("/api/delivery/slots")
class DeliverySlotController {

    record SlotQuery(String pincode, @DateTimeFormat(iso = DateTimeFormat.ISO.DATE) LocalDate date) {}
    record HoldRequest(String cartId) {}
    record HoldView(String holdId, String slotId, String cartId) {}

    private final SlotDelegate delegate;

    DeliverySlotController(SlotDelegate delegate) {
        this.delegate = delegate;
    }

    @GetMapping
    List<SlotView> available(SlotQuery query) {
        return delegate.available(query.pincode(), query.date());
    }

    @PostMapping("/{slotId}/holds")
    ResponseEntity<HoldView> hold(@PathVariable String slotId, @RequestBody HoldRequest req, UriComponentsBuilder uri) {
        String holdId = delegate.hold(slotId, req.cartId());
        return ResponseEntity.created(uri.path("/api/delivery/slots/{slotId}/holds/{holdId}")
                        .buildAndExpand(slotId, holdId).toUri())
                .body(new HoldView(holdId, slotId, req.cartId()));
    }
}
SlotDelegate.java (interface for brevity)
package in.grocery.delivery.delegate;

import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.util.List;

public interface SlotDelegate {
    List<SlotView> available(String pincode, LocalDate date);
    String hold(String slotId, String cartId);    // throws SlotFullException
}
SlotView.java / SlotFullException.java
public record SlotView(String slotId, String window, int remaining) {}

public class SlotFullException extends RuntimeException {
    public SlotFullException(String slotId) { super("Slot " + slotId + " is full"); }
}
SlotExceptionHandler.java
@RestControllerAdvice(assignableTypes = DeliverySlotController.class)
class SlotExceptionHandler {
    @ExceptionHandler
    ProblemDetail full(SlotFullException ex) {
        return ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail(HttpStatus.CONFLICT, ex.getMessage());
    }
}
DeliverySlotControllerTest.java
package in.grocery.delivery.web;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.mockito.BDDMockito.given;

import in.grocery.delivery.delegate.SlotDelegate;
import in.grocery.delivery.delegate.SlotFullException;
import in.grocery.delivery.delegate.SlotView;
import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.util.List;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Autowired;
import org.springframework.boot.test.autoconfigure.web.servlet.WebMvcTest;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Import;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.http.MediaType;
import org.springframework.test.context.bean.override.mockito.MockitoBean;
import org.springframework.test.web.servlet.assertj.MockMvcTester;

@WebMvcTest(DeliverySlotController.class)
@Import(SlotExceptionHandler.class)
class DeliverySlotControllerTest {

    @Autowired MockMvcTester mvc;
    @MockitoBean SlotDelegate delegate;

    @Test
    void listsSlots() {
        given(delegate.available("560034", LocalDate.parse("2026-10-20")))
                .willReturn(List.of(new SlotView("S1", "07:00-09:00", 12)));
        assertThat(mvc.get().uri("/api/delivery/slots?pincode=560034&date=2026-10-20"))
                .hasStatusOk().bodyJson().extractingPath("$[0].slotId").isEqualTo("S1");
    }

    @Test
    void holdReturns201() {
        given(delegate.hold("S1", "c1")).willReturn("H9");
        assertThat(mvc.post().uri("/api/delivery/slots/S1/holds")
                .contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON).content("{\"cartId\":\"c1\"}"))
                .hasStatus(HttpStatus.CREATED)
                .hasHeader("Location", "http://localhost/api/delivery/slots/S1/holds/H9");
    }

    @Test
    void fullSlotIs409() {
        given(delegate.hold("S1", "c1")).willThrow(new SlotFullException("S1"));
        assertThat(mvc.post().uri("/api/delivery/slots/S1/holds")
                .contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON).content("{\"cartId\":\"c1\"}"))
                .hasStatus(HttpStatus.CONFLICT);
    }

    @Test
    void invalidDateIs400() {
        assertThat(mvc.get().uri("/api/delivery/slots?pincode=560034&date=20-10-2026"))
                .hasStatus(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST);
    }
}

Chapter 09 adds @Valid constraints to SlotQuery (pincode format, date not in the past).

docs.title: Key Takeaways
docs.text:
• Spring MVC = DispatcherServlet + handler mappings + adapters + argument resolvers + message converters + exception resolvers.
  • Use correct HTTP semantics: statuses, Location, ETag, conditional requests.
  • Controllers speak HTTP; delegates orchestrate; services decide; repositories persist.
  • Records for DTOs and query objects; stable page contracts; capped sizes; whitelisted sorts.
  • Pick the right hook: filter (raw HTTP), interceptor (handler-aware), argument resolver (context objects), advice (errors/bodies).
  • WebMvcConfigurer, never @EnableWebMvc in Boot apps.
  • Virtual threads make blocking MVC scale; bound downstream resources.
  • Boot 4 brings Jackson 3, Servlet 6.1 and built-in API versioning.

07 Logging · 09 Validation

docs.title: 1. Introduction & Why It Matters
docs.text:
Every value that enters the grocery platform from outside — a quantity typed into the app, a pincode from a delivery form, a GSTIN on a seller's registration, a CSV row from a catalog upload, a Razorpay webhook — is untrusted. Validation is the first line of defence for correctness ("quantity can't be −3"), security (oversized strings, injection payloads, mass assignment) and user experience (clear, field-level messages the Angular form can show next to the right input).

Spring integrates Jakarta Bean Validation (implemented by Hibernate Validator) at every layer:

Where How HTTP request bodies @Valid @RequestBody Path/query/header parameters Constraints directly on controller parameters (built-in method validation since Framework 6.1) Service methods @Validated class + constraints on parameters/return values Configuration properties @Validated @ConfigurationProperties (Chapter 06) JPA entities Validation on persist/update (optional) Programmatic Inject Validator and call it (CSV rows, Kafka messages)

This chapter builds validation for cart, checkout and seller onboarding: built-in and custom Indian constraints (pincode, mobile, GSTIN with checksum), nested and collection validation, groups for create vs update, cross-field rules, method validation in services, localized messages in English and Hindi, and a batch validator for seller CSV uploads. Chapter 10 turns every validation failure into one consistent ProblemDetail response.

docs.title: Who should read which section
docs.text: Band Focus B1 · 0–2 yrs Parts 1, 2, 4 — @Valid, built-in constraints B2 · 2–5 yrs Parts 2, 5 — nested, collections, groups, custom constraints, messages B3 · 5–8 yrs Parts 3, 5, 6 — method validation internals, @Valid vs @Validated, exception types B4 · 8–12 yrs Parts 6, 8 — validation strategy across layers, batch validation, performance B5 · 12–15+ yrs Parts 8, 9 — where rules belong: validation vs domain invariants vs business rules

docs.title: 2.1 Jakarta Bean Validation in one paragraph
docs.text: You annotate fields, record components, parameters or return values with constraints (@NotBlank, @Size, @Pattern...). A Validator checks an object graph against them and returns a set of ConstraintViolations (property path, invalid value, message). Implementation: Hibernate Validator, added by spring-boot-starter-validation.

docs.title: 2.2 Built-in constraints
docs.text:
Constraint Applies to Notes @NotNull Any Null fails @NotEmpty String, Collection, Map, array Null or empty fails @NotBlank String Null, empty or whitespace fails @Size(min, max) String, Collection, Map, array Null is valid @Min, @Max Numbers Long bounds @DecimalMin, @DecimalMax Numbers, numeric strings String bounds, inclusive flag @Positive, @PositiveOrZero, @Negative, @NegativeOrZero Numbers @Digits(integer, fraction) Numbers e.g. money: integer = 8, fraction = 2 @Pattern(regexp) String Whole-string match @Email String Lenient syntax check @Past, @PastOrPresent, @Future, @FutureOrPresent Date/time Uses the validator's clock @AssertTrue, @AssertFalse boolean Useful for cross-field checks @Null Any Must be null (e.g. id on create)

Null is usually valid

Every constraint except the @Not*/@Null family treats null as valid. Combine: @NotNull @Size(max = 100). This composability is deliberate — a constraint checks one thing.

Hibernate Validator adds extras: @Length, @Range, @URL, @UUID, @CreditCardNumber, @ISBN, @CodePointLength...

docs.title: 2.3 Where constraints go
docs.text: Target Example Record component / field record AddItemRequest(@NotBlank String sku, @Min(1) int quantity) Type argument (container element) List<@NotBlank String> tags, Map<@Pattern(...) String, @Positive Integer> Method parameter void reserve(@NotBlank String sku, @Positive int qty) Return value @NotNull Cart get(String id) Class (class-level constraint) @ValidDeliveryWindow class SlotRequest

docs.title: 2.4 Cascading with @Valid
docs.text:
Constraints on nested objects are only checked if the reference is marked @Valid:

CheckoutRequest.java
record CheckoutRequest(@Valid @NotNull Address address, List<@Valid LineItem> items) {}

docs.title: 2.5 @Valid vs @Validated
docs.text: @Valid (Jakarta) @Validated (Spring) Cascade into nested objects ✅ ❌ Trigger validation of @RequestBody/@ModelAttribute ✅ ✅ (and supports groups) Validation groups ❌ ✅ @Validated(OnCreate.class) Enable method validation on a bean (class level) ❌ ✅ Validate @ConfigurationProperties ❌ ✅

docs.title: 2.6 Groups
docs.text:
Groups let the same DTO validate differently per use case: id must be null on create but present on update.

OnCreate.java
public interface OnCreate {}
public interface OnUpdate {}

record SellerRequest(@Null(groups = OnCreate.class) @NotNull(groups = OnUpdate.class) Long id, ...) {}

Constraints without groups belong to Default. @Validated(OnCreate.class) validates only OnCreate unless the group extends Default (interface OnCreate extends Default {}) — a very common surprise. @GroupSequence orders groups so expensive checks run only if cheap ones pass.

docs.title: 2.7 Custom constraints
docs.text: Two parts: an annotation meta-annotated with @Constraint, and a ConstraintValidator. Spring's LocalValidatorFactoryBean creates validators through Spring, so they can inject beans (e.g. a pincode directory). Constraints can also be composed from existing ones without writing a validator.

docs.title: 2.8 Cross-field validation
docs.text:
• @AssertTrue method on the object (simple, local).
  • Class-level custom constraint (reusable, can target a specific property node for the error).

docs.title: 2.9 Method validation
docs.text:
Validates parameters and return values of any Spring bean method:

  • In controllers (Framework 6.1+): if a handler method has constraint annotations directly on parameters (@RequestParam @Pattern(...) String pincode) or @Valid on container elements, Spring MVC applies built-in method validation and raises HandlerMethodValidationException. No @Validated needed on the controller.
  • In other beans: annotate the class with @Validated; Boot's MethodValidationPostProcessor wraps it in an AOP proxy (Chapter 04 rules apply — no self-invocation) and raises ConstraintViolationException.

docs.title: 2.10 Exception types you'll see
docs.text:
Exception When Default status MethodArgumentNotValidException @Valid @RequestBody/@ModelAttribute fails 400 HandlerMethodValidationException Built-in controller method validation fails (6.1+) 400 (or 500 for return values) ConstraintViolationException AOP method validation (@Validated beans) fails 500 unless mapped! BindException / MethodArgumentNotValidException Type conversion/binding errors for model attributes 400 MethodArgumentTypeMismatchException ?quantity=abc for an int param 400 HttpMessageNotReadableException Malformed JSON, wrong type in body 400

The 500 trap

A ConstraintViolationException from a service is not mapped to 400 by default — it becomes a 500. Chapter 10 maps it deliberately. Decide per case whether a service-level violation is a client error (400/422) or a programming error (500).

docs.title: 2.11 Messages and i18n
docs.text: Messages come from interpolated templates: {jakarta.validation.constraints.Size.message} → "size must be between {min} and {max}". Override with the message attribute or keys in ValidationMessages.properties. With Spring, validator messages can also resolve from the app's MessageSource (messages.properties) — Boot wires this — so validation and other UI texts share one set of bundles, localized by Accept-Language.

docs.title: 2.12 Validation vs business rules
docs.text:
Kind Example Where Input validation (syntax, shape) pincode is 6 digits, quantity 1–20 DTO constraints at the edge Domain invariants (always true for a valid object) Money never negative Constructors / value objects Business rules (need state or other data) pincode is serviceable, item in stock, coupon valid for this cart Services, returning domain errors

Don't put database lookups for business rules in constraint validators unless the rule is truly "input validity" and cheap (cached).

docs.title: 3.1 @Valid @RequestBody path
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant HA as RequestMappingHandlerAdapter
    participant RP as RequestResponseBodyMethodProcessor
    participant MC as Jackson HttpMessageConverter
    participant DB as WebDataBinder
    participant V as SpringValidatorAdapter → Hibernate Validator

    HA->>RP: resolveArgument(@Valid AddItemRequest)
    RP->>MC: read body → AddItemRequest
    alt malformed JSON
        MC-->>HA: HttpMessageNotReadableException (400)
    end
    RP->>DB: createBinder(target)
    RP->>DB: validateIfApplicable (sees @Valid / @Validated)
    DB->>V: validate(target, groups)
    V-->>DB: ConstraintViolations → FieldErrors in BindingResult
    alt errors and no BindingResult parameter follows
        RP-->>HA: MethodArgumentNotValidException
    end

The validator is Boot's LocalValidatorFactoryBean (from ValidationAutoConfiguration), wrapped by the MVC WebDataBinder. Violations become Spring FieldErrors with message codes like NotBlank.addItemRequest.sku, NotBlank.sku, NotBlank.java.lang.String, NotBlank — resolvable through MessageSource.

docs.title: 3.2 Built-in controller method validation (Framework 6.1+)
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Handler method registered] --> B{"any parameter has @Constraint<br/>or container elements with constraints?"}
    B -- no --> C[normal argument resolution]
    B -- yes --> D[shouldValidateArguments = true]
    D --> E[resolve all arguments]
    E --> F["MethodValidationAdapter<br/>validate parameters, incl. @RequestParam, @PathVariable, @RequestHeader"]
    F -->|violations| G[HandlerMethodValidationException<br/>ParameterValidationResults per parameter]
    F -->|ok| H[invoke method]
  • If a @RequestBody/@ModelAttribute parameter has only @Valid, it's validated the classic way (MethodArgumentNotValidException). If other parameters also have constraints, all are validated together and everything is reported via HandlerMethodValidationException.
  • Putting @Validated on the controller class also triggers AOP method validation → parameters could be validated twice and throw a different exception. Don't use class-level @Validated on controllers in Framework 6.1+.

docs.title: 3.3 AOP method validation for services
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    C[CheckoutDelegate] --> P[Proxy of InventoryService]
    P --> I[MethodValidationInterceptor]
    I -->|validate parameters<br/>ExecutableValidator| V[Hibernate Validator]
    V -->|violations| X[ConstraintViolationException]
    I -->|ok| T[target.reserve]
    T --> I2[validate return value]

MethodValidationPostProcessor (a BeanPostProcessor from Boot's ValidationAutoConfiguration) proxies every bean annotated @Validated. Self-invocation skips validation, like any AOP.

docs.title: 3.4 Validator bootstrap and injection into validators
docs.text: LocalValidatorFactoryBean configures Hibernate Validator with a SpringConstraintValidatorFactory — constraint validator instances are created via AutowireCapableBeanFactory, so constructor injection works. Validators are cached per constraint annotation instance and must be thread-safe.

docs.title: 4.1 Dependency
docs.text:
build.gradle.kts
implementation(libs.spring.boot.starter.validation)

Without it there's no validator — @Valid silently does nothing (Boot logs nothing about it).

package in.grocery.platform.validation;

import jakarta.validation.Constraint;
import jakarta.validation.Payload;
import jakarta.validation.ReportAsSingleViolation;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.NotNull;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Pattern;
import java.lang.annotation.Documented;
import java.lang.annotation.ElementType;
import java.lang.annotation.Retention;
import java.lang.annotation.RetentionPolicy;
import java.lang.annotation.Target;

@Documented
@NotNull
@Pattern(regexp = "[1-9][0-9]{5}")
@ReportAsSingleViolation                                                              // (1)!
@Constraint(validatedBy = {})                                                         // (2)!
@Target({ElementType.FIELD, ElementType.PARAMETER, ElementType.RECORD_COMPONENT, ElementType.TYPE_USE})
@Retention(RetentionPolicy.RUNTIME)
public @interface Pincode {
    String message() default "{grocery.validation.pincode}";
    Class<?>[] groups() default {};
    Class<? extends Payload>[] payload() default {};
}
  1. One clear message instead of separate "must not be null" + "must match pattern".
  2. Composition only — the meta-constraints do the work.

Constraint with a validator — GSTIN with checksum:

A GSTIN has 15 characters: 2-digit state code, 10-character PAN, entity number, Z, and a check character computed with a weighted mod-36 algorithm.

package in.grocery.platform.validation;

import jakarta.validation.Constraint;
import jakarta.validation.Payload;
import java.lang.annotation.Documented;
import java.lang.annotation.ElementType;
import java.lang.annotation.Retention;
import java.lang.annotation.RetentionPolicy;
import java.lang.annotation.Target;

@Documented
@Constraint(validatedBy = GstinValidator.class)
@Target({ElementType.FIELD, ElementType.PARAMETER, ElementType.RECORD_COMPONENT, ElementType.TYPE_USE})
@Retention(RetentionPolicy.RUNTIME)
public @interface Gstin {
    String message() default "{grocery.validation.gstin}";
    Class<?>[] groups() default {};
    Class<? extends Payload>[] payload() default {};
}
in/grocery/platform/validation/GstinValidator.java
package in.grocery.platform.validation;

import jakarta.validation.ConstraintValidator;
import jakarta.validation.ConstraintValidatorContext;
import java.util.regex.Pattern;

public class GstinValidator implements ConstraintValidator<Gstin, String> {

    private static final Pattern FORMAT =
            Pattern.compile("(0[1-9]|[1-3][0-9])[A-Z]{5}[0-9]{4}[A-Z][1-9A-Z]Z[0-9A-Z]");     // (1)!
    private static final String CHARS = "0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ";

    @Override
    public boolean isValid(String value, ConstraintValidatorContext ctx) {
        if (value == null) return true;                                                        // (2)!
        if (!FORMAT.matcher(value).matches()) return false;
        return checkChar(value) == value.charAt(14);
    }

    static char checkChar(String gstin) {
        int sum = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < 14; i++) {
            int product = CHARS.indexOf(gstin.charAt(i)) * (i % 2 == 0 ? 1 : 2);
            sum += product / 36 + product % 36;
        }
        return CHARS.charAt((36 - sum % 36) % 36);
    }
}
  1. Format: state code, PAN (5 letters, 4 digits, letter), entity number, literal Z, check character. State code range is kept loose (01–39); the tax master decides actual validity.
  2. Null is valid — combine with @NotNull where required (constraint composability).
GstinValidatorTest.java
package in.grocery.platform.validation;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

import org.junit.jupiter.params.ParameterizedTest;
import org.junit.jupiter.params.provider.ValueSource;

class GstinValidatorTest {

    private final GstinValidator validator = new GstinValidator();

    @ParameterizedTest
    @ValueSource(strings = {"27AAPFU0939F1ZV", "29AAGCB7383J1Z4"})
    void acceptsValidGstins(String gstin) {
        assertThat(validator.isValid(gstin, null)).isTrue();
    }

    @ParameterizedTest
    @ValueSource(strings = {
            "27AAPFU0939F1ZX",   // wrong check character
            "27AAPFU0939F1YV",   // 14th char must be Z
            "27aapfu0939f1zv",   // lowercase
            "99AAPFU0939F1ZV",   // invalid state code pattern
            "27AAPFU0939F1Z"     // too short
    })
    void rejectsInvalidGstins(String gstin) {
        assertThat(validator.isValid(gstin, null)).isFalse();
    }
}

Boot's ValidationAutoConfiguration configures the validator to resolve {...} keys through the application MessageSource, and Spring MVC picks the locale from Accept-Language (AcceptHeaderLocaleResolver). Request with Accept-Language: hi-IN → Hindi messages.

Verify

Boot's integration of the application MessageSource into Bean Validation message interpolation has evolved across 3.x versions. If {grocery.validation.pincode} shows up literally, check that ValidationMessages.properties or MessageSource integration is configured for your version (Boot reference Validation).

in/grocery/platform/validation/TimeWindowValidator.java
package in.grocery.platform.validation;

import jakarta.validation.ConstraintValidator;
import jakarta.validation.ConstraintValidatorContext;
import java.time.Duration;

public class TimeWindowValidator implements ConstraintValidator<ValidTimeWindow, TimeWindow> {

    private Duration min;
    private Duration max;

    @Override
    public void initialize(ValidTimeWindow annotation) {
        this.min = Duration.ofMinutes(annotation.minMinutes());
        this.max = Duration.ofMinutes(annotation.maxMinutes());
    }

    @Override
    public boolean isValid(TimeWindow w, ConstraintValidatorContext ctx) {
        if (w == null || w.start() == null || w.end() == null) return true;               // @NotNull handles nulls
        Duration length = Duration.between(w.start(), w.end());
        boolean sameDay = w.start().toLocalDate().equals(w.end().toLocalDate());
        if (!length.isNegative() && sameDay && length.compareTo(min) >= 0 && length.compareTo(max) <= 0) {
            return true;
        }
        ctx.disableDefaultConstraintViolation();                                            // (1)!
        ctx.buildConstraintViolationWithTemplate(ctx.getDefaultConstraintMessageTemplate())
           .addPropertyNode("end")
           .addConstraintViolation();
        return false;
    }
}
  1. Attach the error to the end field so the UI highlights the right input rather than the whole form.
