docs.title: 5.6 Level 3 — Validators that use Spring beans
docs.text:
Pincode format is input validation; existence in India Post's directory is also input validation (it's reference data, cheap if cached) — unlike serviceability, which is a business rule.

in/grocery/platform/validation/KnownPincodeValidator.java
package in.grocery.platform.validation;

import jakarta.validation.ConstraintValidator;
import jakarta.validation.ConstraintValidatorContext;

public class KnownPincodeValidator implements ConstraintValidator<KnownPincode, String> {

    public interface PincodeDirectory { boolean exists(String pincode); }   // in-memory, loaded at startup

    private final PincodeDirectory directory;

    public KnownPincodeValidator(PincodeDirectory directory) {             // (1)!
        this.directory = directory;
    }

    @Override
    public boolean isValid(String value, ConstraintValidatorContext ctx) {
        return value == null || directory.exists(value);
    }
}
  1. Constructor injection works because Spring's LocalValidatorFactoryBean creates validators through the bean factory. The validator is shared across threads — keep it stateless.

Validators outside Spring

Validation.buildDefaultValidatorFactory() (like the unit test in 4.4) can't inject beans and will fail to instantiate this validator. Test it by constructing it directly with a fake directory, or with a Spring-configured validator.

docs.title: 5.7 Level 3 — Method validation in services
Validating seller catalog CSV uploads
docs.text:
Sellers upload catalogs with 5,000–50,000 rows. Requirements:

  • Validate every row with the same constraints as the single-product API.
  • Report all errors with row numbers (not fail on the first), capped at 500 errors.
  • Stream — don't hold the whole file in memory.
  • Reject the file early if the header is wrong.
  • Keep valid rows for import only if the error rate is below 2%.
in/grocery/seller/catalog/ProductRow.java
package in.grocery.seller.catalog;

import jakarta.validation.constraints.DecimalMax;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.DecimalMin;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Digits;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Min;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.NotBlank;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.NotNull;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Pattern;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Size;
import java.math.BigDecimal;

public record ProductRow(
        @NotBlank @Pattern(regexp = "[A-Z0-9-]{3,40}") String sku,
        @NotBlank @Size(max = 150) String name,
        @NotBlank @Pattern(regexp = "[a-z-]{2,40}") String category,
        @NotNull @DecimalMin("0.01") @DecimalMax("999999.99") @Digits(integer = 6, fraction = 2) BigDecimal mrp,
        @NotNull @DecimalMin("0.01") @Digits(integer = 6, fraction = 2) BigDecimal sellingPrice,
        @NotNull @Pattern(regexp = "\\d{4}|\\d{6}|\\d{8}") String hsnCode,
        @NotNull @Min(0) Integer stock) {

    @jakarta.validation.constraints.AssertTrue(message = "selling price must not exceed MRP")
    public boolean isPriceWithinMrp() {                                                     // (1)!
        return mrp == null || sellingPrice == null || sellingPrice.compareTo(mrp) <= 0;
    }
}
  1. Legal requirement in India: selling price can't exceed MRP. The check lives with the data it needs.
in/grocery/seller/catalog/CatalogCsvValidator.java
package in.grocery.seller.catalog;

import jakarta.validation.ConstraintViolation;
import jakarta.validation.Validator;
import java.io.BufferedReader;
import java.io.IOException;
import java.io.InputStream;
import java.io.InputStreamReader;
import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Comparator;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.function.Consumer;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;

@Component
public class CatalogCsvValidator {

    public static final List<String> HEADER =
            List.of("sku", "name", "category", "mrp", "selling_price", "hsn_code", "stock");
    static final int MAX_ERRORS = 500;

    public record RowError(long row, String field, String message, String rejectedValue) {}

    public record Result(long totalRows, long validRows, List<RowError> errors, boolean truncated) {
        public double errorRate() {
            return totalRows == 0 ? 0 : (double) (totalRows - validRows) / totalRows;
        }
        public boolean acceptable() {
            return totalRows > 0 && errorRate() <= 0.02;
        }
    }

    public static class InvalidHeaderException extends RuntimeException {
        public InvalidHeaderException(List<String> actual) { super("Expected header " + HEADER + " but got " + actual); }
    }

    private final Validator validator;                                                       // (1)!

    public CatalogCsvValidator(Validator validator) {
        this.validator = validator;
    }

    public Result validate(InputStream csv, Consumer<ProductRow> validRowSink) throws IOException {
        var reader = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(csv, StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
        String headerLine = reader.readLine();
        List<String> header = headerLine == null ? List.of() : split(stripBom(headerLine));
        if (!header.equals(HEADER)) throw new InvalidHeaderException(header);

        List<RowError> errors = new ArrayList<>();
        long rowNo = 1, total = 0, valid = 0;
        boolean truncated = false;
        String line;
        while ((line = reader.readLine()) != null) {                                          // (2)!
            rowNo++;
            if (line.isBlank()) continue;
            total++;
            List<String> cols = split(line);
            List<RowError> rowErrors = new ArrayList<>();
            ProductRow row = parse(rowNo, cols, rowErrors);
            if (row != null) {
                for (ConstraintViolation<ProductRow> v : validator.validate(row)) {
                    rowErrors.add(new RowError(rowNo, fieldName(v), v.getMessage(), String.valueOf(v.getInvalidValue())));
                }
            }
            if (rowErrors.isEmpty()) {
                valid++;
                validRowSink.accept(row);
            } else if (errors.size() < MAX_ERRORS) {
                rowErrors.sort(Comparator.comparing(RowError::field));                        // deterministic order
                errors.addAll(rowErrors.subList(0, Math.min(rowErrors.size(), MAX_ERRORS - errors.size())));
            } else {
                truncated = true;
            }
        }
        return new Result(total, valid, List.copyOf(errors), truncated);
    }

    private static ProductRow parse(long rowNo, List<String> c, List<RowError> errors) {
        if (c.size() != HEADER.size()) {
            errors.add(new RowError(rowNo, "*", "expected " + HEADER.size() + " columns but found " + c.size(), null));
            return null;
        }
        BigDecimal mrp = decimal(rowNo, "mrp", c.get(3), errors);
        BigDecimal price = decimal(rowNo, "selling_price", c.get(4), errors);
        Integer stock = integer(rowNo, "stock", c.get(6), errors);
        if (!errors.isEmpty()) return null;                                                  // (3)!
        return new ProductRow(c.get(0), c.get(1), c.get(2), mrp, price, c.get(5), stock);
    }

    private static BigDecimal decimal(long row, String field, String raw, List<RowError> errors) {
        try {
            return raw.isBlank() ? null : new BigDecimal(raw.strip());
        } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
            errors.add(new RowError(row, field, "must be a number", raw));
            return null;
        }
    }

    private static Integer integer(long row, String field, String raw, List<RowError> errors) {
        try {
            return raw.isBlank() ? null : Integer.valueOf(raw.strip());
        } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
            errors.add(new RowError(row, field, "must be a whole number", raw));
            return null;
        }
    }

    private static String fieldName(ConstraintViolation<?> v) {
        String path = v.getPropertyPath().toString();
        return switch (path) {
            case "sellingPrice" -> "selling_price";
            case "hsnCode" -> "hsn_code";
            case "priceWithinMrp" -> "selling_price";
            default -> path;
        };
    }

    /** Minimal CSV split supporting quoted fields with commas and doubled quotes. */
    static List<String> split(String line) {
        List<String> out = new ArrayList<>();
        StringBuilder cur = new StringBuilder();
        boolean quoted = false;
        for (int i = 0; i < line.length(); i++) {
            char ch = line.charAt(i);
            if (quoted) {
                if (ch == '"' && i + 1 < line.length() && line.charAt(i + 1) == '"') { cur.append('"'); i++; }
                else if (ch == '"') quoted = false;
                else cur.append(ch);
            } else if (ch == '"') quoted = true;
            else if (ch == ',') { out.add(cur.toString()); cur.setLength(0); }
            else cur.append(ch);
        }
        out.add(cur.toString());
        return out;
    }

    private static String stripBom(String s) {
        return s.startsWith("\uFEFF") ? s.substring(1) : s;                                   // (4)!
    }
}
  1. Inject Spring's Validator (the Jakarta interface) — same configuration, messages and custom validators as the web layer.
  2. Streaming, row by row — memory stays flat for 50,000 rows.
  3. Type conversion errors are reported like validation errors; bean validation runs only on parseable rows.
  4. Excel-exported CSVs often start with a UTF-8 byte-order mark — the header check would fail without this.

Use a real CSV library in production

The hand-written splitter keeps the example dependency-free. For production, use a mature parser (e.g. Apache Commons CSV or FastCSV) — CSV edge cases (multi-line fields, encodings) are endless.

CatalogCsvValidatorTest.java
package in.grocery.seller.catalog;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThatThrownBy;

import jakarta.validation.Validation;
import java.io.ByteArrayInputStream;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

class CatalogCsvValidatorTest {

    private final CatalogCsvValidator validator =
            new CatalogCsvValidator(Validation.buildDefaultValidatorFactory().getValidator());

    private static ByteArrayInputStream csv(String s) {
        return new ByteArrayInputStream(s.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
    }

    @Test
    void reportsRowLevelErrorsAndKeepsValidRows() throws Exception {
        String data = """
                \uFEFFsku,name,category,mrp,selling_price,hsn_code,stock
                ATTA-5KG,"Atta, Whole Wheat 5kg",staples,320.00,289.00,1101,40
                MILK-1L,Toned Milk,dairy,60.00,66.00,0401,100
                ghee 1l,Ghee,dairy,abc,600.00,0405,-1
                """;
        List<ProductRow> valid = new ArrayList<>();

        var result = validator.validate(csv(data), valid::add);

        assertThat(result.totalRows()).isEqualTo(3);
        assertThat(valid).extracting(ProductRow::sku).containsExactly("ATTA-5KG");
        assertThat(result.errors()).extracting(CatalogCsvValidator.RowError::row, CatalogCsvValidator.RowError::field)
                .contains(
                        org.assertj.core.groups.Tuple.tuple(3L, "selling_price"),   // price above MRP
                        org.assertj.core.groups.Tuple.tuple(4L, "mrp"));            // not a number
        assertThat(result.acceptable()).isFalse();
    }

    @Test
    void rejectsWrongHeader() {
        assertThatThrownBy(() -> validator.validate(csv("sku,name\nA,B\n"), r -> {}))
                .isInstanceOf(CatalogCsvValidator.InvalidHeaderException.class);
    }
}

docs.title: Validation performance notes
docs.text: Concern Guidance Validator creation Expensive — use the Spring-managed singleton, never buildDefaultValidatorFactory() per request Regex constraints @Pattern compiles once per constraint; avoid catastrophic backtracking patterns ((a+)+) — attackers can send inputs that take seconds Collections Always bound sizes before @Valid elements; 100,000-element lists validate slowly Validators calling remote services Avoid; use cached reference data Fail-fast mode Hibernate's hibernate.validator.fail_fast=true stops at first violation — cheaper, but worse UX; consider only for internal high-volume paths

docs.title: 7. Spring Boot 3 vs 4 & Migration
Migration checklist
docs.text:
• Remove class-level @Validated from controllers (Framework 6.1+ double validation).
  • Map HandlerMethodValidationException and ConstraintViolationException explicitly (Chapter 10).
  • Re-run validation tests after Hibernate Validator upgrade (message texts may change — don't assert on default messages in contract tests).
  • Check custom ConstraintValidators for Jakarta namespace (Boot 2 → 3).
  • Update imports of ValidationAutoConfiguration in tests for Boot 4.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
1. Validate at the edge — every DTO record has constraints; @Valid on every @RequestBody.
  2. Bound everything — string lengths, collection sizes, numeric ranges.
  3. Custom constraints for domain formats (pincode, mobile, GSTIN, HSN) in the platform library, shared by all services and the CSV validator.
  4. Stable error contract — field paths and message keys (Chapter 10); don't make clients parse English text.
  5. Localize messages via MessageSource keys.
  6. Service-level method validation for contracts called from non-HTTP entry points.
  7. Value objects enforce invariants; validation doesn't replace them.
  8. Business rules return domain errors from services (e.g. PincodeNotServiceable → 422), not constraint violations.

docs.title: Anti-patterns
docs.text:
❌ Manual if validation in controllers

Anti-patterns (snippet)
if (req.quantity() < 1 || req.quantity() > 20) return ResponseEntity.badRequest().body("bad qty");

✅ @Min(1) @Max(20) int quantity + global error handling.

❌ Unbounded strings/lists — String description with no @Size accepts 20 MB of text into your database.

❌ @Validated on controller classes in Framework 6.1+.

❌ Remote calls in validators — latency, failures turn into 500s during validation.

❌ Validating entities as the API contract — couples persistence to input rules.

❌ Leaking internal paths (reserve.arg1[0].quantity) — use -parameters so names are real, and map paths in the error handler.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix @Valid has no effect No validation starter Add spring-boot-starter-validation Nested fields not validated Missing @Valid on the nested reference / type argument Add @Valid Group validation skips normal constraints Group doesn't extend Default interface OnCreate extends Default {} ConstraintViolationException → 500 Not mapped Map in global handler (Chapter 10) Parameter validated twice / different exception types @Validated on controller + 6.1 built-in validation Remove class-level @Validated Message shows {grocery.validation.pincode} Key not found in bundle used by interpolator Put key in ValidationMessages.properties or configure MessageSource integration Validator with injected bean fails in tests Built with Validation.buildDefaultValidatorFactory() Use Spring's validator or construct manually Service method validation ignored Self-invocation / bean not @Validated Call through proxy; annotate class Slow requests with long inputs Regex backtracking Simplify patterns; bound length first with @Size

docs.title: Production checklist
docs.text:
• Every request DTO has constraints and bounds
  • Platform constraints (@Pincode, @IndianMobile, @Gstin, @Hsn) shared
  • Validation exceptions mapped to one error format with field paths
  • Messages externalized and localized
  • No remote calls in validators
  • Batch validators stream and cap error output
  • Constraint tests for each custom validator (valid, invalid, null)

docs.title: B1 · 0–2 years
docs.text:
B1 · How do you validate a request body in Spring Boot?

Short answer: Add spring-boot-starter-validation, put constraints on the DTO fields, and annotate the parameter with @Valid @RequestBody. Failures raise MethodArgumentNotValidException → 400.

B1 · @NotNull vs @NotEmpty vs @NotBlank?

Short answer: @NotNull rejects null. @NotEmpty rejects null or empty (strings, collections). @NotBlank rejects null, empty or whitespace-only strings.

B1 · Is @Size(min = 1) enough to make a field required?

Short answer: No — null is valid for @Size. Combine with @NotNull or use @NotEmpty.

B1 · How do you validate nested objects?

Short answer: Put @Valid on the nested field (or type argument for collection elements).

B1 · What happens if validation dependency is missing?

Short answer: No validator is available; @Valid is silently ignored and invalid data reaches your code.

docs.title: B2 · 2–5 years
docs.text:
B2 · @Valid vs @Validated?

Short answer: @Valid (Jakarta) cascades and triggers validation but has no groups. @Validated (Spring) supports groups, triggers validation of arguments, and at class level enables method validation on beans.

B2 · How do validation groups work and what's the common pitfall?

Short answer: Constraints tagged with groups run only when that group is requested. Pitfall: requesting OnCreate skips all Default constraints unless OnCreate extends Default.

B2 · How do you create a custom constraint?

Short answer: Annotation with @Constraint(validatedBy = X.class), message/groups/payload attributes, plus a ConstraintValidator implementation. Or compose existing constraints with validatedBy = {} and @ReportAsSingleViolation.

B2 · How do you do cross-field validation?

Short answer: @AssertTrue method on the DTO for simple cases, or a class-level custom constraint that attaches the violation to a specific property node.

B2 · How are validation messages localized?

Short answer: Use message keys ({grocery.validation.pincode}) resolved from ValidationMessages/MessageSource bundles per locale (messages_hi.properties), with locale from Accept-Language.

B2 · How do you validate query and path parameters?

Short answer: Put constraints directly on the controller parameters. Framework 6.1+ validates them automatically (HandlerMethodValidationException).

docs.title: B3 · 5–8 years
docs.text:
B3 · Explain the difference between MethodArgumentNotValidException, HandlerMethodValidationException and ConstraintViolationException.

Short answer: MANVE: @Valid body/model attribute validation via WebDataBinder. HMVE: Framework 6.1 built-in method validation of controller parameters. CVE: AOP method validation on @Validated beans (services), not mapped to 400 by default.

B3 · Why shouldn't you put @Validated on controller classes in Spring 6.1+?

Short answer: It adds the AOP method validation interceptor on top of built-in MVC method validation: parameters can be validated twice and failures surface as ConstraintViolationException instead of the MVC exception types your handler expects.

B3 · How can a ConstraintValidator use Spring beans?

Short answer: Spring's LocalValidatorFactoryBean uses SpringConstraintValidatorFactory, creating validators via the bean factory, so constructor injection works. Validators must be thread-safe.

B3 · How does method validation on a service work internally?

Short answer: MethodValidationPostProcessor proxies @Validated beans; MethodValidationInterceptor uses the ExecutableValidator to check parameters before and return values after invocation, throwing ConstraintViolationException. Subject to proxy limitations.

B3 · How do you validate a CSV of 50,000 rows efficiently?

Short answer: Stream rows, map to a record, validate with the shared singleton Validator, collect errors with row numbers up to a cap, handle conversion errors separately, and decide acceptance by error rate. Bound file size up front.

docs.title: B4 · 8–12 years
docs.text:
B4 · Where should different kinds of rules live?

Short answer: Input shape/format at the edge (constraints), invariants in value objects/aggregates, stateful business rules in services with domain errors, cross-service rules in orchestration/sagas. Keep validators free of remote calls.

B4 · How do you design a validation error contract for web and mobile clients?

Short answer: RFC 9457 problem details with a stable code, and an errors array of {field, code, message} where field is a JSON path matching the request and code a stable key clients can map; message localized server-side for display. Version it like the API.

B4 · What are the security aspects of validation?

Short answer: Bound sizes (DoS), safe regexes (ReDoS), whitelist enums/sort fields, prevent mass assignment by using dedicated DTOs, validate on the server regardless of client checks, and never interpolate user input into messages unsafely (Hibernate Validator EL expression injection in custom messages — don't put user input into message templates).

docs.title: B5 · 12–15+ years
docs.text:
B5 · How would you share validation rules between Angular, Flutter and Spring?

Short answer: Server is authoritative. Publish constraints via OpenAPI (patterns, lengths, enums) and generate client validators; keep India-specific formats in a shared spec; accept that complex rules live only server-side and return field-level errors clients render.

B5 · A team wants to validate stock availability in a @InStock constraint. Your view?

Short answer: No — it's a stateful business rule needing a remote/DB call, race-prone and not "input validity". It belongs in the reservation service with a domain error (409/422) and should be enforced at reservation time, not validation time.

docs.title: Scenario questions
docs.text:
Scenario · A mobile app release causes a spike of 500s on checkout

New app sends couponCodes: null → service-level @Validated rejects @NotNull on the list → ConstraintViolationException → unmapped → 500. Fixes: map CVE (400 for edge-origin data), make couponCodes optional in the DTO with a default empty list, contract tests with the app's payloads, and alert on 5xx caused by validation.

Scenario · A seller uploads a CSV and the API takes 40 seconds and times out

File had a description column with 100 KB HTML per row and a @Pattern with nested quantifiers → catastrophic backtracking. Fix: @Size limits before pattern constraints, safer regex, max file size, async import with job status, and per-row time limits.

docs.title: Coding exercise
docs.text:
Exercise · @HsnCode and @ValidCoupon

  1. Create @HsnCode (4, 6 or 8 digits) as a composed constraint.
  2. Create a class-level @ValidCouponRequest for record CouponRequest(String code, BigDecimal cartTotal, BigDecimal minOrder) requiring cartTotal >= minOrder, reporting the error on cartTotal. Test both.
Solution HsnCode.java
package in.grocery.platform.validation;

import jakarta.validation.Constraint;
import jakarta.validation.Payload;
import jakarta.validation.ReportAsSingleViolation;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Pattern;
import java.lang.annotation.ElementType;
import java.lang.annotation.Retention;
import java.lang.annotation.RetentionPolicy;
import java.lang.annotation.Target;

@Pattern(regexp = "\\d{4}|\\d{6}|\\d{8}")
@ReportAsSingleViolation
@Constraint(validatedBy = {})
@Target({ElementType.FIELD, ElementType.PARAMETER, ElementType.RECORD_COMPONENT, ElementType.TYPE_USE})
@Retention(RetentionPolicy.RUNTIME)
public @interface HsnCode {
    String message() default "HSN code must have 4, 6 or 8 digits";
    Class<?>[] groups() default {};
    Class<? extends Payload>[] payload() default {};
}
ValidCouponRequest.java + validator
package in.grocery.promotion.web;

import jakarta.validation.Constraint;
import jakarta.validation.ConstraintValidator;
import jakarta.validation.ConstraintValidatorContext;
import jakarta.validation.Payload;
import java.lang.annotation.ElementType;
import java.lang.annotation.Retention;
import java.lang.annotation.RetentionPolicy;
import java.lang.annotation.Target;
import java.math.BigDecimal;

@Constraint(validatedBy = ValidCouponRequest.Validator.class)
@Target(ElementType.TYPE)
@Retention(RetentionPolicy.RUNTIME)
public @interface ValidCouponRequest {
    String message() default "cart total is below the coupon's minimum order value";
    Class<?>[] groups() default {};
    Class<? extends Payload>[] payload() default {};

    class Validator implements ConstraintValidator<ValidCouponRequest, CouponRequest> {
        @Override
        public boolean isValid(CouponRequest r, ConstraintValidatorContext ctx) {
            if (r == null || r.cartTotal() == null || r.minOrder() == null) return true;
            if (r.cartTotal().compareTo(r.minOrder()) >= 0) return true;
            ctx.disableDefaultConstraintViolation();
            ctx.buildConstraintViolationWithTemplate(ctx.getDefaultConstraintMessageTemplate())
               .addPropertyNode("cartTotal").addConstraintViolation();
            return false;
        }
    }
}

@ValidCouponRequest
record CouponRequest(@jakarta.validation.constraints.NotBlank String code,
                     @jakarta.validation.constraints.NotNull BigDecimal cartTotal,
                     @jakarta.validation.constraints.NotNull BigDecimal minOrder) {}
CouponValidationTest.java
package in.grocery.promotion.web;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

import in.grocery.platform.validation.HsnCode;
import jakarta.validation.Validation;
import jakarta.validation.Validator;
import java.math.BigDecimal;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

class CouponValidationTest {

    private final Validator validator = Validation.buildDefaultValidatorFactory().getValidator();

    record Item(@HsnCode String hsn) {}

    @Test
    void hsnCode() {
        assertThat(validator.validate(new Item("0401"))).isEmpty();
        assertThat(validator.validate(new Item("04011"))).hasSize(1);
    }

    @Test
    void couponBelowMinimumReportedOnCartTotal() {
        var violations = validator.validate(new CouponRequest("DIWALI100", new BigDecimal("450"), new BigDecimal("499")));
        assertThat(violations).singleElement()
                .extracting(v -> v.getPropertyPath().toString()).isEqualTo("cartTotal");
    }
}

docs.title: Key Takeaways
docs.text:
• Jakarta Bean Validation + Hibernate Validator, enabled by spring-boot-starter-validation.
  • Constraints on records, type arguments, parameters, return values, classes; @Valid to cascade.
  • Groups need extends Default to include normal constraints — or use separate DTOs.
  • Custom constraints (composed or with validators) for India-specific formats; validators can inject beans.
  • Framework 6.1+ validates controller parameters built-in (HandlerMethodValidationException); don't add @Validated to controllers.
  • Service method validation via @Validated beans throws ConstraintViolationException — map it deliberately.
  • Keep input validation, invariants and business rules in their proper places.
  • Batch validation: stream, cap errors, handle conversion errors, reuse the singleton validator.

docs.text:
• Spring Framework Reference — Core › Validation, Data Binding, and Type Conversion › Java Bean Validation; Web MVC › Validation

  • GST portal documentation on GSTIN structure

08 REST APIs with Spring MVC · 10 Error Handling & Problem Details

docs.title: 1. Introduction & Why It Matters
docs.text:
When the checkout call fails, three audiences read the response:

  • The Angular and Flutter apps need a machine-readable code to decide what to do: show "This pincode isn't serviceable yet", highlight the mobile field, refresh a stale cart, or retry later.
  • The customer needs a human, localized message — in English or Hindi — not NullPointerException at CartService.java:142.
  • The on-call engineer needs a trace ID that leads straight to logs and traces, and a clean split between "client did something wrong" (4xx, no alert) and "we broke" (5xx, alert).

Without a standard, every service invents its own error JSON: {"error": "..."} here, {"message": ..., "status": ...} there, HTML Whitelabel pages from filters, and stack traces leaking internal class names to attackers.

RFC 9457 Problem Details (successor of RFC 7807) is the IETF standard for HTTP API errors, and Spring supports it natively with ProblemDetail, ErrorResponse and ErrorResponseException. This chapter builds the grocery platform's single error contract: a domain exception hierarchy with an error-code catalog, one global handler covering validation, framework, domain and unexpected errors, consistent output even for errors in filters, localized messages, correct logging levels, and translation of downstream service errors.

docs.title: Who should read which section
docs.text: Band Focus B1 · 0–2 yrs Parts 1, 2, 4 — @ExceptionHandler, @RestControllerAdvice, status codes B2 · 2–5 yrs Parts 2, 5 — ProblemDetail, validation errors, ResponseEntityExceptionHandler B3 · 5–8 yrs Parts 3, 5, 6 — exception resolver chain, /error fallback, filter errors, i18n B4 · 8–12 yrs Parts 6, 7, 8 — platform error contract, downstream error translation, observability B5 · 12–15+ yrs Parts 8, 9 — error design as API governance

docs.title: 2.1 RFC 9457 Problem Details
docs.text:
Media type application/problem+json. Standard members:

Member Meaning Grocery example type URI identifying the problem type (documentation link) https://errors.grocery.in/pincode-not-serviceable title Short, human summary of the type (stable) Pincode not serviceable status HTTP status code 422 detail Human explanation of this occurrence We don't deliver to 744101 yet instance URI of this occurrence (usually request path) /api/checkout Extensions Any extra members code, traceId, errors, retryAfter

type defaults to about:blank (meaning "the status code says it all").

docs.title: 2.2 Spring's building blocks
docs.text:
Type Role ProblemDetail The body object: type, title, status, detail, instance, properties map for extensions ErrorResponse Interface for exceptions that know their status, headers and ProblemDetail; supports message codes for i18n ErrorResponseException Base class implementing ErrorResponse — extend it for exceptions that carry their own problem ResponseStatusException Quick exception with status + reason (implements ErrorResponse) @ExceptionHandler Method handling specific exception types @ControllerAdvice / @RestControllerAdvice Global (or scoped) holder of exception handlers ResponseEntityExceptionHandler Base advice class handling all Spring MVC exceptions as ProblemDetail — extend and override spring.mvc.problemdetails.enabled Boot registers a ResponseEntityExceptionHandler advice for you

All Spring MVC framework exceptions (MethodArgumentNotValidException, HttpRequestMethodNotSupportedException, NoResourceFoundException, HttpMediaTypeNotSupportedException, …) implement ErrorResponse in Framework 6+.

docs.title: 2.3 Where errors can originate — and who handles them
docs.text: Origin Handled by Controller / delegate / service / repository (during handler execution) @ExceptionHandler in controller or advice → HandlerExceptionResolvers Argument resolution / validation / message conversion Same (inside DispatcherServlet) Interceptors (preHandle) Same Servlet filters (before DispatcherServlet) Not your @ControllerAdvice — container error dispatch to /error → Boot's BasicErrorController Spring Security filters Security's AuthenticationEntryPoint / AccessDeniedHandler (Chapter 17) Async (StreamingResponseBody, DeferredResult) Advice for async dispatch; partial responses can't be replaced once committed Response already committed Nothing can change the status — log and close

docs.title: 2.4 Boot's /error fallback
docs.text:
When an exception escapes the DispatcherServlet (or response.sendError(...) is called), the servlet container forwards to /error. Boot's BasicErrorController renders JSON (or the Whitelabel HTML page for browsers) using ErrorAttributes. Relevant properties:

application.yml
server:
  error:
    include-stacktrace: never     # never expose in production
    include-message: never        # exception messages can leak internals
    include-binding-errors: never
    include-exception: false
    whitelabel:
      enabled: false

docs.title: 2.5 Status code decisions
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Error occurred] --> B{Client's fault?}
    B -- yes --> C{Which?}
    C --> C1[400 malformed / invalid input]
    C --> C2[401 not authenticated]
    C --> C3[403 authenticated but not allowed]
    C --> C4[404 not found / hidden]
    C --> C5[409 conflicts with current state]
    C --> C6[412/428 preconditions]
    C --> C7[422 valid input, violates business rule]
    C --> C8[429 rate limited]
    B -- no --> D{Our fault or dependency?}
    D --> D1[500 bug / unexpected]
    D --> D2[502 bad response from upstream]
    D --> D3[503 temporarily unavailable / overloaded]
    D --> D4[504 upstream timeout]

4xx: don't alert, do measure. 5xx: alert.

docs.title: 2.6 Error codes
docs.text: HTTP status is too coarse ("422" could mean 20 different business failures). Each problem gets a stable, documented code in the code extension, e.g. CART_ITEM_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, PINCODE_NOT_SERVICEABLE, PAYMENT_DECLINED. Clients switch on code, never on detail text.

docs.title: 2.7 Internationalization
docs.text:
ErrorResponse exposes message codes Spring resolves through MessageSource:

Code Resolves problemDetail.type.<exception FQN> type problemDetail.title.<exception FQN> title problemDetail.<exception FQN> detail (with arguments)

ResponseEntityExceptionHandler is MessageSourceAware and uses them. You can also resolve messages yourself in the handler from your error-code catalog.

docs.title: 3.1 The exception resolver chain
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant DS as DispatcherServlet
    participant C as HandlerExceptionResolverComposite
    participant EH as ExceptionHandlerExceptionResolver
    participant RS as ResponseStatusExceptionResolver
    participant DH as DefaultHandlerExceptionResolver
    participant Ctr as Servlet container
    participant BEC as BasicErrorController (/error)

    DS->>DS: exception from handler / arg resolution / interceptor
    DS->>C: processHandlerException
    C->>EH: 1. @ExceptionHandler in controller, then @ControllerAdvice beans (ordered)
    alt handled
        EH-->>DS: ModelAndView (body written via converters)
    else not handled
        C->>RS: 2. @ResponseStatus on exception class / ResponseStatusException
        C->>DH: 3. standard Spring MVC exceptions → status via sendError
    end
    alt still unhandled or sendError called
        DS-->>Ctr: exception propagates / error status set
        Ctr->>BEC: ERROR dispatch to /error
        BEC-->>Ctr: JSON from ErrorAttributes
    end
  • ExceptionHandlerExceptionResolver finds the best-matching @ExceptionHandler by exception type distance (closest superclass wins). It checks the controller class first, then @ControllerAdvice beans in @Order order. It also matches root causes if the top-level exception doesn't match.
  • Handler methods can return ProblemDetail, ErrorResponse, ResponseEntity<ProblemDetail> — written via message converters with application/problem+json.
  • DefaultHandlerExceptionResolver calls response.sendError(status) — which triggers the container's /error dispatch. With problem details enabled (advice extending ResponseEntityExceptionHandler), those exceptions are handled earlier as ProblemDetail instead.

docs.title: 3.2 ResponseEntityExceptionHandler
docs.text:
A base class with one @ExceptionHandler method covering ~20 Spring MVC exception types. For each, it calls a protected handleXxx(...) method you can override, which by default builds the exception's ProblemDetail and calls handleExceptionInternal(...) → createResponseEntity(...). Override points:

  • handleMethodArgumentNotValid — add field errors.
  • handleHandlerMethodValidationException — add parameter errors.
  • handleExceptionInternal — add common extensions (trace ID, code) to every framework problem.

docs.title: 3.3 ProblemDetail serialization
docs.text: Jackson serializes ProblemDetail with a mixin (ProblemDetailJacksonMixin in Spring Web) that flattens properties into top-level members — so problem.setProperty("code", "X") appears as "code": "X", per the RFC. Boot 4's Jackson 3 support provides the equivalent mixin.

docs.title: 4.1 A local @ExceptionHandler
4.2 Global handling with @RestControllerAdvice
4.3 Turn on problem details for framework errors
docs.text:
application.yml
spring:
  mvc:
    problemdetails:
      enabled: true

Now a 405, 415, malformed JSON or validation failure also returns application/problem+json instead of Boot's default error JSON.

docs.title: 4.4 Exceptions that carry their own problem
5.1 Level 2 — Extending ResponseEntityExceptionHandler for field errors
5.2 Level 2 — Parameter validation and ConstraintViolationException
5.3 Level 2 — Logging by severity
5.4 Level 3 — Errors raised in filters
docs.text:
A request with an invalid X-Request-Id or a rejected API key fails in a filter — before the DispatcherServlet. Your advice never sees it; the container forwards to /error and Boot's BasicErrorController answers with a different JSON shape.

Option A — delegate to the MVC exception resolvers from the filter:

in/grocery/platform/web/ApiKeyFilter.java
package in.grocery.platform.web;

import jakarta.servlet.FilterChain;
import jakarta.servlet.ServletException;
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest;
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletResponse;
import java.io.IOException;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.web.filter.OncePerRequestFilter;
import org.springframework.web.server.ResponseStatusException;
import org.springframework.web.servlet.HandlerExceptionResolver;

public class ApiKeyFilter extends OncePerRequestFilter {

    public interface ApiKeyChecker { boolean valid(String key); }

    private final ApiKeyChecker checker;
    private final HandlerExceptionResolver resolver;                                     // (1)!

    public ApiKeyFilter(ApiKeyChecker checker, HandlerExceptionResolver resolver) {
        this.checker = checker;
        this.resolver = resolver;
    }

    @Override
    protected void doFilterInternal(HttpServletRequest req, HttpServletResponse res, FilterChain chain)
            throws ServletException, IOException {
        String key = req.getHeader("X-Seller-Api-Key");
        if (key == null || !checker.valid(key)) {
            resolver.resolveException(req, res, null,
                    new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.UNAUTHORIZED, "Missing or invalid seller API key")); // (2)!
            return;
        }
        chain.doFilter(req, res);
    }

    @Override
    protected boolean shouldNotFilter(HttpServletRequest request) {
        return !request.getRequestURI().startsWith("/api/seller-integrations/");
    }
}
  1. Inject the handlerExceptionResolver bean (qualifier "handlerExceptionResolver") — the composite used by the DispatcherServlet, including your advice.
  2. The same global handler formats the problem — one error contract everywhere.

Option B — make /error produce the same shape by providing a custom ErrorAttributes or your own ErrorController (Level 4 does this as a safety net).

docs.title: 5.5 Level 3 — Localized titles and details via message codes
docs.text:
messages.properties

For an ErrorResponseException, pass detailMessageArguments (the {0}) via the constructor that accepts messageDetailCode and arguments, or override getDetailMessageArguments(). ResponseEntityExceptionHandler resolves them using the request locale. Level 4 uses the same idea with the error-code catalog instead of class names, which survives refactoring.

Every error from every service

docs.title: 6.1 Error-code catalog
6.2 Domain exceptions — HTTP-free
6.3 Downstream errors
docs.text:
When pricing-service or Razorpay fails, translate at the client boundary (Chapter 19) into a platform exception:

in/grocery/platform/error/DependencyException.java
package in.grocery.platform.error;

public class DependencyException extends RuntimeException {

    private final String dependency;
    private final ErrorCode code;

    public DependencyException(String dependency, ErrorCode code, String message, Throwable cause) {
        super(message, cause);
        this.dependency = dependency;
        this.code = code;
    }

    public String dependency() { return dependency; }
    public ErrorCode code() { return code; }

    public static DependencyException timeout(String dependency, Throwable cause) {
        return new DependencyException(dependency, ErrorCode.DEPENDENCY_TIMEOUT, dependency + " timed out", cause);
    }

    public static DependencyException unavailable(String dependency, Throwable cause) {
        return new DependencyException(dependency, ErrorCode.DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE, dependency + " unavailable", cause);
    }
}

Never proxy downstream error bodies

Passing pricing-service's problem (or Razorpay's error payload) straight to the customer leaks internals and couples clients to internal services. Translate: map known downstream codes to your own codes, everything else to DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE.

docs.title: 6.4 The global handler
6.5 Safety net: consistent /error output
docs.text:
Anything that still reaches /error (filters not using the resolver, container-level errors) should look the same:

in/grocery/platform/error/GroceryErrorController.java
package in.grocery.platform.error;

import jakarta.servlet.RequestDispatcher;
import jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest;
import java.net.URI;
import java.time.Clock;
import org.springframework.boot.web.servlet.error.ErrorController;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.http.MediaType;
import org.springframework.http.ProblemDetail;
import org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

@RestController
public class GroceryErrorController implements ErrorController {                          // (1)!

    private final Clock clock;

    public GroceryErrorController(Clock clock) {
        this.clock = clock;
    }

    @RequestMapping("/error")
    ResponseEntity<ProblemDetail> error(HttpServletRequest request) {
        Object statusAttr = request.getAttribute(RequestDispatcher.ERROR_STATUS_CODE);
        HttpStatus status = statusAttr instanceof Integer s ? HttpStatus.resolve(s) : null;
        if (status == null) status = HttpStatus.INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR;
        ErrorCode code = status.is5xxServerError() ? ErrorCode.INTERNAL_ERROR
                : status == HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND ? ErrorCode.NOT_FOUND : ErrorCode.MALFORMED_REQUEST;

        ProblemDetail pd = ProblemDetail.forStatus(status);
        pd.setType(code.type());
        pd.setTitle(status.getReasonPhrase());
        Object uri = request.getAttribute(RequestDispatcher.ERROR_REQUEST_URI);
        if (uri != null) pd.setInstance(URI.create(uri.toString()));
        pd.setProperty("code", code.name());
        pd.setProperty("retryable", code.retryable());
        pd.setProperty("timestamp", clock.instant().toString());
        pd.setProperty("errors", java.util.List.of());
        return ResponseEntity.status(status).contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_PROBLEM_JSON).body(pd);
    }
}
  1. Defining your own ErrorController makes Boot's BasicErrorController back off. The package of ErrorController may change in Boot 4 — verify.

docs.title: 6.6 Contract tests
6.7 Documenting errors
docs.text: Generate an error catalog page from ErrorCode + message bundles at build time and publish it at https://errors.grocery.in/ (this handbook's appendix can include it). In OpenAPI (Chapter 20), declare application/problem+json responses with the shared Problem schema for each operation's possible codes.

docs.text:
Topic Boot 3.5 / Framework 6.2 Boot 4.x / Framework 7 ProblemDetail, ErrorResponse ✅ (since 6.0) ✅ RFC reference RFC 9457 (7807 in early 6.0 docs) RFC 9457 Problem JSON serialization Jackson 2 mixin Jackson 3 support (verify custom serializers of ProblemDetail) spring.mvc.problemdetails.enabled ✅ ✅ (verify property after modularization) HandlerMethodValidationException accessors 6.1/6.2 API Check for deprecations/renames ErrorController, ErrorAttributes packages org.springframework.boot.web.servlet.error Moved into web modules (verify) @MockBean in error tests Deprecated Removed — use @MockitoBean Spring Boot 3.5Spring Boot 4.x Spring Boot 3.5 (snippet)

import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.ObjectMapper;   // in tests parsing problems
Spring Boot 4.x (snippet)

docs.title: Migration checklist
docs.text:
• One ResponseEntityExceptionHandler subclass per app; remove duplicates.
  • Replace custom error JSON formats with ProblemDetail + extensions; version the contract for clients.
  • Update handler code for HandlerMethodValidationException API changes.
  • Re-run error contract tests after Jackson 3 upgrade (property flattening, date formats).
  • Check custom ErrorController/ErrorAttributes imports.
  • server.error.include-* settings reviewed.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
1. One error format (RFC 9457 + code, traceId, timestamp, errors, retryable) for every response, including filter and /error paths.
  2. Stable error-code catalog as an enum with documentation; clients switch on code.
  3. HTTP-free domain exceptions, mapped once in the platform handler.
  4. Never expose exception messages or stack traces for 5xx; detail for 4xx comes from message bundles.
  5. Log by severity: 5xx ERROR with stack, dependency WARN, 4xx DEBUG; count all via metrics.
  6. Translate downstream errors; add Retry-After where retry makes sense.
  7. Localize titles/details by Accept-Language.
  8. Contract tests for the error format.

docs.title: Anti-patterns
docs.text:
❌ catch (Exception e) { return ResponseEntity.status(500).body(e.getMessage()); } in controllers — leaks internals, bypasses logging and format.

❌ 200 with error body ({"success": false}) — breaks HTTP semantics, caches, monitoring.

❌ Different error JSON per service — clients write 26 parsers.

❌ Exceptions for flow control with full stack traces in hot paths — use lightweight domain exceptions.

❌ Swallowing exceptions (catch (Exception e) {}) or logging and returning null.

❌ Leaking existence — 403 for "cart belongs to someone else" confirms the cart exists; use 404.

❌ Relying on detail text in clients — it's localized and may change.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Whitelabel HTML page or Boot default JSON Error escaped MVC (filter) / sendError / problem details disabled Resolver delegation in filters; custom ErrorController; enable problem details Advice not applied Advice outside scanned packages; scoped basePackages; another advice with higher precedence handles it Check scanning and @Order Wrong handler chosen Handler for superclass in higher-precedence advice Order advices; specific handlers in the same advice ConstraintViolationException → 500 Not mapped Add handler Validation errors missing field details Default ProblemDetail of MANVE Override handleMethodArgumentNotValid properties nested instead of flattened Custom ObjectMapper without Spring's problem mixin Use Boot's mapper/customizers Localized messages not applied Bundle not in spring.messages.basename; wrong encoding Configure basenames and UTF-8 Status 200 with error body in streaming download Response already committed Validate before streaming; handle errors inside stream by aborting connection

docs.title: Production checklist
docs.text:
• Platform handler registered in every service (via platform auto-configuration)
  • server.error.include-* = never; Whitelabel disabled
  • Filters delegate errors to HandlerExceptionResolver
  • Error-code catalog documented and published
  • traceId present in all problems
  • Error metrics by code; alerts on 5xx rate and dependency error rate
  • Contract tests for problem format, including i18n

docs.title: B1 · 0–2 years
docs.text:
B1 · What does @ExceptionHandler do?

Short answer: Marks a method that handles a specific exception type thrown by controller methods, producing the response.

B1 · @ControllerAdvice vs @RestControllerAdvice?

Short answer: Both hold global handlers; @RestControllerAdvice adds @ResponseBody, so return values are serialized to the body.

B1 · What is RFC 9457 Problem Details?

Short answer: A standard JSON format (application/problem+json) for HTTP API errors with type, title, status, detail, instance, plus extensions.

B1 · Which status for a validation failure? For a missing resource? For an unexpected bug?

Short answer: 400 (or 422 for business-rule violations), 404, 500.

B1 · Why shouldn't you return exception messages to clients?

Short answer: They can leak internals (SQL, class names, secrets) and aren't user-friendly or localized.

docs.title: B2 · 2–5 years
docs.text:
B2 · How do you enable ProblemDetail responses for Spring MVC exceptions?

Short answer: spring.mvc.problemdetails.enabled=true, or register an advice extending ResponseEntityExceptionHandler.

B2 · How do you add field-level validation errors to the problem?

Short answer: Extend ResponseEntityExceptionHandler, override handleMethodArgumentNotValid, add an errors extension from the binding result.

B2 · What is ErrorResponseException?

Short answer: A base exception implementing ErrorResponse that carries its own status, headers and ProblemDetail; Spring renders it without a custom handler.

B2 · How are handlers matched when several could handle an exception?

Short answer: Controller-local handlers first, then advices by order; within an advice the closest exception type in the hierarchy wins; root causes are also considered.

B2 · What should be logged for 4xx vs 5xx?

Short answer: 4xx: little or nothing (debug), counted via metrics. 5xx: ERROR with stack trace, alerts.

docs.title: B3 · 5–8 years
docs.text:
B3 · Describe the HandlerExceptionResolver chain.

Short answer: ExceptionHandlerExceptionResolver (@ExceptionHandlers in controller/advices), ResponseStatusExceptionResolver (@ResponseStatus, ResponseStatusException), DefaultHandlerExceptionResolver (standard exceptions via sendError). Unhandled → container error dispatch to /error.

B3 · Why don't exceptions thrown in filters reach @ControllerAdvice?

Short answer: Filters run before the DispatcherServlet; advices are part of MVC's exception resolution. Delegate to the HandlerExceptionResolver from the filter or customize /error.

B3 · How does Spring localize ProblemDetail fields?

Short answer: ErrorResponse exposes message codes (problemDetail.type.*, problemDetail.title.*, problemDetail.*) resolved via MessageSource by ResponseEntityExceptionHandler, using the request locale.

B3 · How are ProblemDetail properties serialized at top level?

Short answer: Spring registers a Jackson mixin that unwraps the properties map into top-level members.

B3 · When can't you change the error status?

Short answer: Once the response is committed (streaming, flushed buffer). Validate before streaming; on mid-stream failure, abort the connection and log.

docs.title: B4 · 8–12 years
docs.text:
B4 · Design an error contract for 26 services and two client apps.

Short answer: RFC 9457 plus code, traceId, timestamp, errors, retryable; central ErrorCode catalog with docs and localized messages; HTTP-free domain exceptions; platform handler and /error controller; downstream translation; metrics; contract tests; versioned evolution (add codes, never change meaning).

B4 · How do you handle errors from downstream services?

Short answer: Translate at the client boundary into platform exceptions; map known codes to your own; treat unknown as dependency failure (502/503/504) with Retry-After; never proxy bodies; combine with timeouts, retries and circuit breakers (Chapter 26).

B4 · Why use lightweight exceptions for domain rejections?

Short answer: Stack trace capture is costly; under load (sale spikes with many out-of-stock rejections) it adds CPU and GC pressure. Business rejections don't need traces; unexpected errors do.

docs.title: B5 · 12–15+ years
docs.text:
B5 · How do error codes evolve without breaking clients?

Short answer: Codes are append-only; meanings never change; clients must handle unknown codes by status-class fallback; deprecate with documentation and telemetry; new specific codes can refine old generic ones only with client compatibility (e.g. keep status and add subCode).

B5 · How do errors connect to SLOs?

Short answer: Availability SLOs count 5xx (and sometimes 429/timeouts) as bad events; 4xx generally don't burn the budget, except client-visible failures caused by us (e.g. 409 from our own race conditions). Error codes let you classify precisely and alert on budget burn rate.

docs.title: Scenario questions
docs.text:
Scenario · The Flutter app shows 'Something went wrong' for out-of-stock items

order-service returned 409 with a legacy {error: "OOS"} body from a local handler that shadowed the platform handler (higher precedence advice). The app parses code and fell back to generic text. Fix: remove the local handler; throw OutOfStockException; add a contract test; lint for @ExceptionHandler outside the platform package.

Scenario · A security scan finds stack traces in API responses

Errors thrown in a custom rate-limit filter reached /error, and server.error.include-stacktrace=on_param let ?trace=true expose traces. Fix: include-stacktrace=never in platform defaults, filter delegates to resolver, custom ErrorController safety net, and a test hitting a filter error.

docs.title: Coding exercise
docs.text:
Exercise · Payment declined mapping

Razorpay returns declines with codes like BAD_REQUEST_ERROR and reasons like payment_failed / insufficient_funds. Create PaymentDeclinedException(String reason) mapping to PAYMENT_DECLINED (422) with detail "Your payment was declined: {reason}" and a declineReason extension; unknown gateway errors should become PAYMENT_GATEWAY_UNAVAILABLE (503). Write a translator method and tests.

Solution PaymentDeclinedException.java
package in.grocery.payment.service;

import in.grocery.platform.error.DomainException;
import in.grocery.platform.error.ErrorCode;
import java.util.Map;

public final class PaymentDeclinedException extends DomainException {
    private final String reason;

    public PaymentDeclinedException(String reason) {
        super(ErrorCode.PAYMENT_DECLINED, "declined: " + reason, humanize(reason));
        this.reason = reason;
    }

    @Override
    public Map<String, Object> extensions() {
        return Map.of("declineReason", reason);
    }

    private static String humanize(String reason) {
        return switch (reason) {
            case "insufficient_funds" -> "insufficient funds";
            case "payment_failed" -> "the bank could not process the payment";
            default -> "please try another payment method";
        };
    }
}
RazorpayErrorTranslator.java
package in.grocery.payment.client;

import in.grocery.payment.service.PaymentDeclinedException;
import in.grocery.platform.error.DependencyException;
import in.grocery.platform.error.ErrorCode;
import java.util.Set;

public final class RazorpayErrorTranslator {

    private static final Set<String> DECLINES = Set.of("payment_failed", "insufficient_funds", "card_declined");

    private RazorpayErrorTranslator() {}

    public static RuntimeException translate(int httpStatus, String errorCode, String reason) {
        if ("BAD_REQUEST_ERROR".equals(errorCode) && reason != null && DECLINES.contains(reason)) {
            return new PaymentDeclinedException(reason);
        }
        return new DependencyException("razorpay", ErrorCode.PAYMENT_GATEWAY_UNAVAILABLE,
                "razorpay error status=" + httpStatus + " code=" + errorCode, null);
    }
}
RazorpayErrorTranslatorTest.java
package in.grocery.payment.client;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

import in.grocery.payment.service.PaymentDeclinedException;
import in.grocery.platform.error.DependencyException;
import in.grocery.platform.error.ErrorCode;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

class RazorpayErrorTranslatorTest {

    @Test
    void knownDeclineBecomesDomainError() {
        var ex = RazorpayErrorTranslator.translate(400, "BAD_REQUEST_ERROR", "insufficient_funds");
        assertThat(ex).isInstanceOf(PaymentDeclinedException.class);
        assertThat(((PaymentDeclinedException) ex).extensions()).containsEntry("declineReason", "insufficient_funds");
    }

    @Test
    void unknownErrorBecomesDependencyFailure() {
        var ex = RazorpayErrorTranslator.translate(500, "SERVER_ERROR", null);
        assertThat(ex).isInstanceOf(DependencyException.class);
        assertThat(((DependencyException) ex).code()).isEqualTo(ErrorCode.PAYMENT_GATEWAY_UNAVAILABLE);
    }
}

DependencyException needs its code included in respond(...) → 503 with Retry-After. Add Hindi text for error.PAYMENT_DECLINED.*.

docs.title: Key Takeaways
docs.text:
• RFC 9457 ProblemDetail is Spring's native error body; extend it with code, traceId, timestamp, errors, retryable.
  • Resolver chain: @ExceptionHandler (controller → advices) → @ResponseStatus/ResponseStatusException → defaults → /error.
  • Extend ResponseEntityExceptionHandler once, and use handleExceptionInternal to enrich every framework error.
  • Filters and /error need explicit handling to keep one format.
  • HTTP-free domain exceptions + error-code catalog + localized messages = clean layers and stable client contracts.
  • Log 5xx loudly, 4xx quietly, count everything with metrics.
  • Translate downstream errors; never proxy them.

docs.text:

  • Spring Boot Reference — Web › Servlet › Error Handling
  • Spring Framework Javadoc — ResponseEntityExceptionHandler, ErrorResponse, HandlerMethodValidationException

09 Validation · 11 JSON & Serialization

docs.title: 1. Introduction & Why It Matters
docs.text:
JSON is the wire format between every part of the grocery platform: Angular and Flutter clients, 26 services, Kafka events (Chapter 23), Redis caches (Chapter 21), Razorpay webhooks and seller integrations. Spring Boot uses Jackson for all of it, and most of the time it "just works" — until it doesn't:

  • A price 289.00 arrives in the Angular app as 289 and the invoice shows "₹289" instead of "₹289.00"; worse, 0.1 + 0.2 rounding bugs appear when JavaScript sums line totals.
  • A delivery slot starting at 7:00 a.m. IST is shown as 1:30 a.m. because the server serialized LocalDateTime without an offset and the app assumed UTC.
  • Adding a new OrderStatus.PACKED enum value crashes every mobile app installed before the release, because their JSON parser rejects the unknown value.
  • A seller-facing endpoint accidentally exposes costPrice because someone added a getter to a DTO.
  • A payload with 100,000 nested arrays pins a CPU core — a denial of service in 2 KB.

And there's a version shift: Spring Boot 4 moves to Jackson 3 — new Maven coordinates, new package names, immutable mappers, unchecked exceptions and some changed defaults.

This chapter covers Jackson in Spring Boot deeply: how Boot configures it, records and naming, dates and money, views and polymorphism, custom serializers, security limits, streaming, and a platform JSON module that works across Boot 3.5 and 4.x.

docs.title: Who should read which section
docs.text: Band Focus B1 · 0–2 yrs Parts 1, 2, 4 — records to JSON, annotations, spring.jackson.* B2 · 2–5 yrs Parts 2, 5 — dates, money, enums, naming strategies, custom serializers, @JsonTest B3 · 5–8 yrs Parts 3, 5, 6 — how Boot builds the mapper, polymorphism, views, streaming B4 · 8–12 yrs Parts 6, 7, 8 — platform JSON contract, Jackson 3 migration, security constraints B5 · 12–15+ yrs Parts 8, 9 — schema evolution and compatibility across clients and events

docs.title: 2.1 Jackson building blocks
docs.text:
Concept Jackson 2 (Boot 3.5) Jackson 3 (Boot 4.x) Group ID (core, databind) com.fasterxml.jackson.core tools.jackson.core Package com.fasterxml.jackson.databind tools.jackson.databind Annotations com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation unchanged (jackson-annotations stays in the 2.x line) Mapper ObjectMapper (mutable, configurable after creation) JsonMapper built via JsonMapper.builder(); immutable Exceptions JsonProcessingException (checked) JacksonException (unchecked) Java time, Optional, parameter names Separate modules (jsr310, jdk8, parameter-names) Built in Serializer base types JsonSerializer, JsonDeserializer, SerializerProvider ValueSerializer, ValueDeserializer, SerializationContext Dates default Boot disables timestamp dates → ISO strings ISO strings by default

Annotations didn't move

@JsonProperty, @JsonIgnore, @JsonInclude, @JsonTypeInfo keep their com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation package in Jackson 3. DTOs that only use annotations usually compile unchanged. Custom serializers, modules and mapper configuration are what need migration.

Verify

Jackson 3 renamed many methods (e.g. generator "field" methods to "property"/"name" variants) and changed some default features. Check the Jackson 3 migration guide and the Spring Boot 4 Jackson section before porting custom code.

docs.title: 2.2 How Boot configures Jackson
docs.text:
Boot auto-configures one shared mapper used by Spring MVC message converters, RestClient/WebClient, Actuator and (by convention) your own code. It applies:

  • spring.jackson.* properties.
  • All registered Modules (beans), @JsonComponent/@JacksonComponent serializers and @JsonMixin/@JacksonMixin mixins.
  • Customizer beans (Jackson2ObjectMapperBuilderCustomizer in Boot 3; JsonMapperBuilderCustomizer in Boot 4).
  • Sensible defaults: FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES disabled, dates as ISO strings, default view inclusion disabled.

Always inject the Boot-managed mapper; never new ObjectMapper() in application code.

docs.title: 2.3 Common properties
docs.text: Property Example Effect spring.jackson.default-property-inclusion non_null Omit null fields spring.jackson.serialization.* indent_output: true SerializationFeatures spring.jackson.deserialization.* fail_on_unknown_properties: false DeserializationFeatures spring.jackson.mapper.* accept_case_insensitive_enums: true MapperFeatures spring.jackson.property-naming-strategy SNAKE_CASE Global naming (rarely wise) spring.jackson.time-zone Asia/Kolkata Zone for java.util.Date-style types spring.jackson.date-format — For legacy Date only

docs.title: 2.4 Records and naming
docs.text:
Records serialize by component name: record CartLine(String sku, int quantity) ↔ {"sku": ..., "quantity": ...}. Deserialization uses the canonical constructor (parameter names via -parameters or record metadata). Rename with @JsonProperty("unit_price") on the component.

Naming strategy per DTO (@JsonNaming(SnakeCaseStrategy.class)) is better than a global strategy: our API is camelCase, Razorpay's is snake_case.

docs.title: 2.5 Inclusion, ignoring, ordering
docs.text: Annotation Use @JsonInclude(NON_NULL / NON_EMPTY / NON_ABSENT) Omit null/empty values @JsonIgnore Never (de)serialize a property @JsonIgnoreProperties(ignoreUnknown = true) Tolerate extra fields (Boot already does globally) @JsonProperty(access = READ_ONLY) Serialize but don't accept from input @JsonPropertyOrder Stable field order (helps diffs and signatures) @JsonUnwrapped Flatten nested object @JsonAnySetter / @JsonAnyGetter Dynamic properties

docs.title: 2.6 Dates and times — the platform rules
docs.text: Java type JSON Use for Instant "2026-09-22T05:35:14.231Z" Event/audit timestamps (always UTC) OffsetDateTime "2026-10-20T07:00:00+05:30" Customer-facing times (slots) — offset is explicit LocalDate "2026-10-20" Calendar dates (delivery date, date of birth) LocalTime "07:00" Store opening hours Duration "PT30M" Durations LocalDateTime ❌ avoid in APIs Ambiguous — which zone? java.util.Date ❌ legacy —

docs.title: 2.7 Money
docs.text:
JSON numbers are IEEE-754 doubles in JavaScript: 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.30000000000000004. For money, choose one:

Option Example Notes Decimal string "289.00" Exact, keeps scale; clients parse with a decimal library Integer minor units 28900 (paise) Exact; Razorpay uses this Plain JSON number 289.00 → often 289 ❌ scale lost; float math in JS

The grocery API uses decimal strings for customer-facing money and paise integers for payment-gateway integrations.

docs.title: 2.8 Enums and forward compatibility
docs.text:
Clients and consumers must survive new enum values. On the reading side:

  • @JsonEnumDefaultValue on an UNKNOWN constant + READ_UNKNOWN_ENUM_VALUES_USING_DEFAULT_VALUE, or
  • READ_UNKNOWN_ENUM_VALUES_AS_NULL.

On the writing side, document that enums are open — clients must handle unknown values.

docs.title: 2.9 Views
docs.text: @JsonView(Views.Seller.class) on properties + on the controller method = different projections of one class. Useful, but separate DTOs are usually clearer and safer — a forgotten @JsonView exposes data.

docs.title: 2.10 Polymorphism
docs.text:
@JsonTypeInfo + @JsonSubTypes (or sealed types) serialize a type discriminator. Use logical names (use = Id.NAME), never class names (Id.CLASS) for untrusted input.

Default typing is a remote-code-execution risk

activateDefaultTyping(...) / enableDefaultTyping() lets the payload choose which Java class to instantiate. Combined with "gadget" classes on the classpath, attackers get RCE — a long series of Jackson CVEs came from this. Never enable it for data from outside your trust boundary. If a cache needs it (e.g. GenericJackson2JsonRedisSerializer), use a strict PolymorphicTypeValidator — or typed serializers (Chapter 21).

docs.title: 2.11 Custom serializers and modules
docs.text:
• Serializer/deserializer classes registered via a Module or @JsonComponent/@JacksonComponent.
  • Mixins — add annotations to classes you don't own (@JsonMixin(ThirdPartyClass.class)).
  • @JsonValue / @JsonCreator — simplest way to make a value type serialize as a single value.

docs.title: 2.12 Read constraints
docs.text: Jackson 2.15+ enforces StreamReadConstraints (max nesting depth, number length, string length, document length in newer versions). Tighten them for public endpoints; loosen only for trusted bulk imports.

docs.title: 2.13 Alternatives
docs.text: Boot also supports Gson and JSON-B (Yasson) as message converters (spring.mvc.converters.preferred-json-mapper). Mixing mappers across services leads to subtle contract differences — standardize on Jackson.

docs.title: 3.1 From HTTP body to record and back
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant RP as RequestResponseBodyMethodProcessor
    participant MC as Jackson message converter
    participant M as Boot-configured JsonMapper/ObjectMapper
    participant P as JsonParser (streaming)
    participant D as Deserializer (BeanDeserializer / record creator)

    RP->>MC: canRead(AddItemRequest, application/json)?
    RP->>MC: read(type, inputMessage)
    MC->>M: readValue(stream, JavaType)
    M->>P: tokenize (StreamReadConstraints enforced)
    M->>D: find/cached deserializer for type
    D->>D: match properties → constructor params (records)<br/>convert values (String→Instant, BigDecimal...)
    D-->>RP: AddItemRequest
    Note over RP: validation (Chapter 09) then handler runs
    RP->>MC: write(CartView, application/json)
    MC->>M: writeValue(out, value) with view/filters
    M-->>RP: bytes to response
  • Serializers/deserializers are resolved once per type and cached in the mapper — the reason a mapper must be shared, and why configuring it after first use (Jackson 2) is dangerous.
  • Records are handled via their canonical constructor as a "properties-based creator".
  • Errors: malformed JSON → HttpMessageNotReadableException (cause: JsonParseException, MismatchedInputException, InvalidFormatException) → 400 via Chapter 10's handler.

docs.title: 3.2 How Boot assembles the mapper
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[JacksonAutoConfiguration] --> B[builder bean<br/>Boot 3: Jackson2ObjectMapperBuilder<br/>Boot 4: JsonMapper.Builder]
    B --> C[StandardJackson2ObjectMapperBuilderCustomizer / Boot 4 equivalent<br/>applies spring.jackson.* properties]
    B --> D[user customizers<br/>ordered]
    B --> E["Module beans + JsonComponentModule<br/>@JsonComponent / @JacksonComponent classes"]
    B --> F["mixins from @JsonMixin / @JacksonMixin scan"]
    B --> G["ObjectMapper / JsonMapper bean<br/>@Primary, @ConditionalOnMissingBean"]
    G --> H[MVC message converters]
    G --> I[RestClient / WebClient codecs]
    G --> J[Actuator, your beans]

If you define your own ObjectMapper bean, Boot's backs off — and you lose all of the above unless you build yours from Boot's builder.

docs.title: 3.3 ProblemDetail and other framework types
docs.text: Spring registers mixins for its own types (e.g. ProblemDetail's flattened properties, Chapter 10). A hand-built mapper without them produces a different error JSON — another reason to use Boot's.

4.2 Global defaults via properties
docs.text:
application.yml
spring:
  jackson:
    default-property-inclusion: non_null

docs.title: 4.3 Using the shared mapper in code
4.4 Testing JSON with @JsonTest
5.1 Level 2 — Money as a value type
docs.text:
The Money record from Chapter 01 should appear in JSON as "289.00".

in/grocery/common/money/Money.java (JSON-aware)
package in.grocery.common.money;

import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonCreator;
import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonValue;
import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.math.RoundingMode;
import java.util.Objects;

public record Money(BigDecimal amount) implements Comparable<Money> {

    public Money {
        Objects.requireNonNull(amount, "amount");
        if (amount.signum() < 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Money cannot be negative: " + amount);
        amount = amount.setScale(2, RoundingMode.HALF_UP);
    }

    @JsonCreator                                                       // (1)!
    public static Money parse(String value) {
        return new Money(new BigDecimal(value.strip()));
    }

    @JsonValue                                                         // (2)!
    public String asString() {
        return amount.toPlainString();
    }

    public Money plus(Money other) { return new Money(amount.add(other.amount)); }

    @Override
    public int compareTo(Money o) { return amount.compareTo(o.amount); }
}
  1. Delegating creator: JSON string → Money. Also accepts numbers written as strings.
  2. Single-value serialization: "289.00" — scale always preserved, no exponent (toPlainString).

Annotations in a shared library

Putting @JsonValue/@JsonCreator in grocery-common adds a dependency on jackson-annotations only (small, stable, and the same package in Jackson 2 and 3). If you want the domain completely framework-free, use a mixin (5.3) instead.

docs.title: 5.2 Level 2 — Time zones done right
5.3 Level 2 — Mixins for classes you don't own
docs.text:
A shared Pincode value class lives in grocery-common, and we want it as a plain string in JSON without adding annotations to the domain:

in/grocery/platform/json/PincodeMixin.java
package in.grocery.platform.json;

import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonCreator;
import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonValue;
import in.grocery.common.address.Pincode;
import org.springframework.boot.jackson.JsonMixin;                       // Boot 4: @JacksonMixin (verify)

@JsonMixin(Pincode.class)                                              // (1)!
abstract class PincodeMixin {

    @JsonCreator
    PincodeMixin(String value) {}

    @JsonValue
    abstract String value();
}
  1. Boot scans @JsonMixin classes in the application packages and registers them with the mapper.

docs.title: 5.4 Level 2 — Forward-compatible enums
5.5 Level 2 — Per-client naming: Razorpay's snake_case
5.6 Level 3 — Polymorphic webhook events
docs.text:
Razorpay sends events with a discriminator field "event": payment.captured, payment.failed, refund.processed, and more over time.

in/grocery/payment/webhook/RazorpayWebhook.java
package in.grocery.payment.webhook;

import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonIgnoreProperties;
import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonSubTypes;
import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonTypeInfo;
import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.PropertyNamingStrategies;
import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.annotation.JsonNaming;

@JsonTypeInfo(
        use = JsonTypeInfo.Id.NAME,                                          // (1)!
        include = JsonTypeInfo.As.EXISTING_PROPERTY,
        property = "event",
        visible = true,
        defaultImpl = RazorpayWebhook.Unknown.class)                         // (2)!
@JsonSubTypes({
        @JsonSubTypes.Type(value = RazorpayWebhook.PaymentCaptured.class, name = "payment.captured"),
        @JsonSubTypes.Type(value = RazorpayWebhook.PaymentFailed.class, name = "payment.failed"),
        @JsonSubTypes.Type(value = RazorpayWebhook.RefundProcessed.class, name = "refund.processed")
})
@JsonIgnoreProperties(ignoreUnknown = true)
public sealed interface RazorpayWebhook {

    String event();

    @JsonNaming(PropertyNamingStrategies.SnakeCaseStrategy.class)
    record PaymentEntity(String id, String orderId, long amount, String currency, String status,
                         String method, String errorCode, String errorReason) {}

    @JsonNaming(PropertyNamingStrategies.SnakeCaseStrategy.class)
    record RefundEntity(String id, String paymentId, long amount, String status) {}

    record PaymentWrapper(PaymentEntity entity) {}
    record RefundWrapper(RefundEntity entity) {}

    record PaymentPayload(PaymentWrapper payment) {}
    record RefundPayload(RefundWrapper refund, PaymentWrapper payment) {}

    record PaymentCaptured(String event, PaymentPayload payload, long createdAt) implements RazorpayWebhook {}
    record PaymentFailed(String event, PaymentPayload payload, long createdAt) implements RazorpayWebhook {}
    record RefundProcessed(String event, RefundPayload payload, long createdAt) implements RazorpayWebhook {}
    record Unknown(String event) implements RazorpayWebhook {}
}
  1. Logical names, a closed list of subtypes — safe polymorphism.
  2. New event types (e.g. payment.dispute.created) map to Unknown instead of failing. We acknowledge them (so Razorpay stops retrying) and log for follow-up.
in/grocery/payment/webhook/WebhookDispatcher.java
public WebhookOutcome dispatch(RazorpayWebhook hook) {
    return switch (hook) {                                                   // exhaustive over the sealed type
        case RazorpayWebhook.PaymentCaptured c -> payments.markCaptured(
                c.payload().payment().entity().orderId(), c.payload().payment().entity().id(),
                c.payload().payment().entity().amount());
        case RazorpayWebhook.PaymentFailed f -> payments.markFailed(
                f.payload().payment().entity().orderId(), f.payload().payment().entity().errorReason());
        case RazorpayWebhook.RefundProcessed r -> refunds.markProcessed(r.payload().refund().entity().id());
        case RazorpayWebhook.Unknown u -> WebhookOutcome.ignored(u.event());
    };
}

Verify the signature before parsing

Webhooks must be authenticated by verifying the X-Razorpay-Signature HMAC over the raw request body bytes before deserializing. Read the body as byte[]/String, verify, then parse with the mapper. Re-serializing a parsed object changes bytes and breaks the signature. (Chapter 18.)

docs.title: 5.7 Level 3 — JSON views vs separate DTOs
5.8 Level 3 — Streaming large JSON
docs.text:
Exporting 200,000 order lines for a seller's monthly report must not build a giant list in memory.

Spring Boot 3.5 (Jackson 2)Spring Boot 4.x (Jackson 3) Streaming large JSON (snippet)
@GetMapping(value = "/api/sellers/{sellerId}/reports/orders", produces = MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON_VALUE)
StreamingResponseBody export(@PathVariable String sellerId) {
    return out -> {
        try (JsonGenerator gen = mapper.getFactory().createGenerator(out);
             Stream<OrderLineRow> rows = reports.streamOrderLines(sellerId)) {   // JDBC stream, Chapter 12
            gen.writeStartArray();
            rows.forEach(row -> {
                try {
                    mapper.writeValue(gen, row);                                   // one object at a time
                } catch (IOException e) {
                    throw new UncheckedIOException(e);
                }
            });
            gen.writeEndArray();
        }
    };
}
Streaming large JSON (snippet)
@GetMapping(value = "/api/sellers/{sellerId}/reports/orders", produces = MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON_VALUE)
StreamingResponseBody export(@PathVariable String sellerId) {
    return out -> {
        try (JsonGenerator gen = mapper.createGenerator(out);                      // tools.jackson.core.JsonGenerator
             Stream<OrderLineRow> rows = reports.streamOrderLines(sellerId)) {
            gen.writeStartArray();
            rows.forEach(row -> mapper.writeValue(gen, row));                      // unchecked exceptions
            gen.writeEndArray();
        }
    };
}

For machine consumers, NDJSON (application/x-ndjson, one object per line) is even simpler to produce and consume incrementally.

docs.title: Platform JSON module
docs.text:
Requirements for every grocery service:

  1. Money as decimal strings; Paise (long) for gateway DTOs.
  2. @Sensitive fields masked when serialized for logs and audit (not for API responses — a dedicated mapper).
  3. Tight StreamReadConstraints for public APIs.
  4. Unknown enum values → default; unknown properties tolerated.
  5. The same behaviour on Boot 3.5 (Jackson 2) and Boot 4.x (Jackson 3).
